drugs.name: Cefazolin
drugs.use: Surgical prophylaxis, within 60 min of incision
drugs.note: 30 mg/kg to a maximum of 2 g (3 g from 120 kg in adults), redosed every 4 hours of surgery, per the ASHP/IDSA/SIS/SHEA 2013 guideline as reproduced in open sources; follow your institution's antimicrobial protocol.
drugs.source: Bratzler DW, et al. Am J Health Syst Pharm 2013;70:195–283 (via secondary sources)

localAnesthetics.name: Bupivacaine HCl
localAnesthetics.note: Label: 175 mg plain, 225 mg with epinephrine 1:200,000, 400 mg in 24 hours, repeatable every 3 hours; no per-kg figure — the 2.5 mg/kg ceiling applied here below those caps is convention. Not recommended under 12 years by the label; 2.5 mg/kg is the ASRA/ESRA pediatric single-injection maximum. 0.75% is not for obstetric anesthesia; no Bier block.
localAnesthetics.source: Marcaine / Marcaine with Epinephrine label (Hospira), revised 7/2023; ASRA/ESRA 2018 (Suresh S, et al. Reg Anesth Pain Med 2018;43:211–216)

localAnesthetics.name: 2-Chloroprocaine
localAnesthetics.note: Label: 11 mg/kg to 800 mg plain, 14 mg/kg to 1,000 mg with epinephrine (added by the clinician, 0.1 mL of 1:1,000 per 20 mL); children over 3 years 11 mg/kg. Nesacaine is not for spinal use; Clorotekal 1% is the intrathecal product (50 mg).

localAnesthetics.name: Exparel (liposomal bupivacaine)
localAnesthetics.note: Adults: up to 266 mg (20 mL of 13.3 mg/mL) by infiltration; 133 mg for interscalene, popliteal sciatic and adductor canal blocks (adductor canal admixed with 50 mg of 0.5% bupivacaine HCl). Children 6 to under 17 years: 4 mg/kg to 266 mg, infiltration only. May be diluted with preservative-free saline or lactated Ringer's to 0.89 mg/mL (never water). Bupivacaine HCl may be mixed in the same syringe if its milligram dose does not exceed half the Exparel dose; no admixture with other agents; give Exparel 20 minutes or more after lidocaine; avoid additional local anesthetics for 96 hours. Not for epidural, intrathecal, intravascular or intra-articular use.

localAnesthetics.name: Lidocaine HCl
localAnesthetics.note: Label: 4.5 mg/kg to 300 mg plain, 7 mg/kg to 500 mg with epinephrine, for healthy adults, with reduced doses for children (the same per-kg figures are applied here); Bier block 3 mg/kg in children with 0.5% plain only. Methylparaben vials are not for neuraxial use.

localAnesthetics.name: Mepivacaine HCl
localAnesthetics.note: Label: usually not more than 400 mg; 7 mg/kg (550 mg) only in exceptional circumstances; 1,000 mg in 24 hours; repeat no sooner than 90 minutes. Children 5–6 mg/kg, and under 3 years or 14 kg use concentrations below 2%. No epinephrine product outside dentistry; not for spinal use.

localAnesthetics.name: Ropivacaine HCl
localAnesthetics.note: Label: major nerve block 75–300 mg (0.75%, 10–40 mL; 0.5%, 175–250 mg), with caution at 300 mg; infiltration 5–200 mg; 770 mg over 24 hours tolerated for postoperative analgesia; no per-kg figure — 3 mg/kg below the 300 mg cap is convention; epinephrine does not limit absorption. Pediatric safety not established by the label; ASRA/ESRA caudal maximum 2 mg/kg (epidural 1.7 mg/kg, peripheral blocks 0.5–1.5 mg/kg).

neuraxial.source: Kopp SL, et al. Regional anesthesia in the patient receiving antithrombotic or thrombolytic therapy: ASRA Pain Medicine evidence-based guidelines (fifth edition). Reg Anesth Pain Med 2025. doi:10.1136/rapm-2024-105766
general: The same intervals apply to neuraxial blocks and to deep plexus or deep peripheral blocks (stellate, infraclavicular, lumbar plexus, lumbar sympathetic, paravertebral); for other peripheral blocks weigh the site's compressibility, vascularity and the consequences of bleeding.
Review the chart daily for every other hemostasis-altering drug: effects add up. With a catheter on LMWH, no concomitant antiplatelet drugs, standard heparin, dextran or oral anticoagulants.

PT/INR and aPTT do not measure a DOAC. For apixaban, rivaroxaban and edoxaban a drug-calibrated level below 30 ng/mL or an anti-Xa at or below 0.1 IU/mL permits a block before the full hold; for dabigatran only a level below 30 ng/mL (diluted thrombin time) does.

Reversal with idarucizumab, andexanet alfa, PCC or aPCC just to permit a block is advised against in routine patients. A bloody tap does not mandate cancelling surgery: discuss it with the surgeon; with LMWH, delay the first postoperative dose to 24 hours.
Platelet count before a neuraxial technique after more than 4 days of heparin or LMWH.

Parturients: the same recommendations apply; for a select high-risk parturient on VTE prophylaxis who needs an urgent intervention, general anesthesia may carry the greater risk and an exception may be appropriate after multidisciplinary discussion.
Dose each agent as the FDA label directs; the low and high tiers follow the label's indications, not the patient's reason for the drug.

drugs.name: Heparin, subcutaneous

tiers.label: Low dose: 5,000 units two or three times daily
tiers.catheter: May stay; remove 4–6 h after the last dose
tiers.restartText: Next dose immediately after catheter removal

tiers.label: High dose: 7,500–10,000 units twice daily (up to 20,000 units/day)
tiers.catheter: Safety of a catheter above 5,000 units per dose or 15,000 units/day is not established: individual decision with neurologic monitoring
tiers.restartText: Not specified by the guideline

tiers.label: High dose: more than 10,000 units per dose or 20,000 units/day
tiers.catheter: As for the lower high-dose tier
tiers.restartText: Not specified by the guideline

notes: Platelet count after more than 4 days of heparin.

drugs.name: Heparin, intravenous infusion

tiers.label: Therapeutic infusion or intraoperative heparinization
tiers.holdText: Stop the infusion 4–6 h and confirm normal coagulation (aPTT)
tiers.catheter: May stay with postoperative heparinization: remove 4–6 h after the last dose once coagulation is normal, using minimal local-anesthetic concentrations and motor checks. Not suggested with full anticoagulation for cardiac surgery
tiers.restartText: Intraoperative heparin no sooner than 1 h after needle placement; reheparinize no sooner than 1 h after catheter removal

notes: A bloody or difficult placement does not mandate cancelling: discuss with the surgeon.

drugs.name: LMWH (enoxaparin, dalteparin, tinzaparin)

tiers.label: Low dose: enoxaparin 40 mg daily or 30 mg twice daily; dalteparin 5,000 IU daily
tiers.level: Inside 12 h, consider an anti-Xa level; at or below 0.1 IU/mL is acceptable before the block (new in 2025)
tiers.catheter: Once-daily regimen: may stay, remove 12 h after the last dose. Twice-daily regimen: remove before the first dose
tiers.restartText: First dose 12 h or more after placement (twice-daily regimen: the next day); once-daily regimen: second dose no sooner than 24 h after the first; next dose 4 h after catheter removal

tiers.label: High dose: enoxaparin 1 mg/kg twice daily or 1.5 mg/kg daily; dalteparin 120 IU/kg twice daily or 200 IU/kg daily; tinzaparin 175 IU/kg daily
tiers.level: Inside 24 h, consider an anti-Xa level, particularly over 75 years or with CrCl at or below 30 mL/min; at or below 0.1 IU/mL is acceptable
tiers.catheter: Remove 4 h before the first postoperative dose
tiers.restartText: First dose 24 h after placement (48–72 h after high-bleeding-risk surgery) and 4 h after removal, whichever is later
tiers.renalNote: Halve the last preoperative dose when CrCl is below 50 mL/min

notes: Routine anti-Xa monitoring is not recommended (it does not predict bleeding), but a level inside the interval may be checked in the elderly, the morbidly obese or with severe renal insufficiency; at or below 0.1 IU/mL counts as no effect.
Platelet count after more than 4 days.
With a catheter in place, no antiplatelet drugs, standard heparin or dextran, whatever the LMWH regimen.

drugs.name: Warfarin

tiers.label: Any dose
tiers.holdText: Stop 5 days before and document a normal INR; if a first dose was given more than 24 h earlier, or a second dose, check the INR
tiers.catheter: May stay on low-dose warfarin with a daily INR and sensory-motor checks; hold or reduce the dose if INR is above 3; remove when INR is below 1.5 (1.5–3: with caution). No recommendation exists for removal at therapeutic anticoagulation
tiers.restartText: No dosing interval; neurologic checks for 48 h after removal

notes: Urgent reversal: vitamin K, PCC or rFVIIa rather than FFP.

drugs.name: Apixaban

tiers.label: High dose: 5 mg twice daily (10 mg twice daily in the first 7 days of VTE treatment; 2.5 mg twice daily when dose-reduced for stroke prevention)
tiers.level: Level below 30 ng/mL or anti-Xa ≤ 0.1 IU/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: No dosing with a catheter in place. If a dose is given inadvertently, withhold 72 h, or document a level below 30 ng/mL (anti-Xa at or below 0.1 IU/mL), before removing it

tiers.label: Low dose: 2.5 mg twice daily for VTE prophylaxis
tiers.level: Level below 30 ng/mL or anti-Xa ≤ 0.1 IU/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: No dosing with a catheter in place. If a dose is given inadvertently, withhold 36 h, or document a level below 30 ng/mL (anti-Xa at or below 0.1 IU/mL), before removing it

notes: After a traumatic (bloody) puncture the label delays the next dose 48 h (manufacturer, not graded).

drugs.name: Rivaroxaban

tiers.label: High dose: 15–20 mg daily (15 mg twice daily in the first 21 days of VTE treatment)
tiers.level: Level below 30 ng/mL or anti-Xa ≤ 0.1 IU/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: No dosing with a catheter in place. If a dose is given inadvertently, withhold 72 h, or document a level below 30 ng/mL (anti-Xa at or below 0.1 IU/mL), before removing it

tiers.label: Low dose: 10 mg daily, or 2.5 mg twice daily with aspirin for CAD or PAD
tiers.level: Level below 30 ng/mL or anti-Xa ≤ 0.1 IU/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: No dosing with a catheter in place. If a dose is given inadvertently, withhold 24 h (30 h if CrCl is below 30 mL/min), or document a level below 30 ng/mL (anti-Xa at or below 0.1 IU/mL), before removing it

notes: After a traumatic (bloody) puncture the label delays the next dose 24 h (manufacturer, not graded).

drugs.name: Edoxaban

tiers.label: 30–60 mg daily
tiers.level: Level below 30 ng/mL or anti-Xa ≤ 0.1 IU/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: No dosing with a catheter in place. If a dose is given inadvertently, withhold 72 h, or document a level below 30 ng/mL (anti-Xa at or below 0.1 IU/mL), before removing it

notes: No recommendation for low-dose edoxaban (no FDA indication).
No manufacturer delay is stated after a traumatic puncture.

drugs.name: Dabigatran

tiers.label: Treatment or stroke-prevention dosing: 150 mg twice daily (75 mg twice daily at CrCl 15–30 mL/min)

renal.label: CrCl below 30 mL/min
renal.text: Avoid the block unless the dabigatran level is below 30 ng/mL (TT or dTT, not aPTT)

tiers.level: Level below 30 ng/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: No dosing with a catheter in place. If a dose is given inadvertently, withhold 72 h (120 h if CrCl 30–49 mL/min), or document a dabigatran level below 30 ng/mL, before removing it

tiers.label: VTE-prophylaxis dosing: 110 mg on day 1, then 220 mg daily

renal.label: CrCl below 30 mL/min
renal.text: Avoid the block unless the level is below 30 ng/mL

tiers.level: Level below 30 ng/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: No dosing with a catheter in place. If a dose is given inadvertently, withhold 48 h, or document a dabigatran level below 30 ng/mL, before removing it

notes: Dabigatran is measured by the diluted thrombin time (a normal thrombin time excludes it); anti-Xa does not apply. No manufacturer delay is stated after a traumatic puncture.

drugs.name: Fondaparinux

tiers.label: Low dose: 2.5 mg daily
tiers.level: A fondaparinux-calibrated anti-Xa ≤ 0.1 IU/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: Not addressed as a maintenance regimen; remove 6 h before the next dose
tiers.restartText: Next dose 6 h after catheter removal

tiers.label: High dose: 5–10 mg daily

renal.label: CrCl 30–50 mL/min (no separate interval given: consider a calibrated anti-Xa)
CrCl below 30 mL/min
renal.text: No neuraxial or deep block: fondaparinux is contraindicated below 30 mL/min (half-life 72 h)

tiers.level: A fondaparinux-calibrated anti-Xa ≤ 0.1 IU/mL permits an earlier block
tiers.catheter: Remove before dosing
tiers.restartText: First postoperative dose 6 h after catheter removal

notes: Contraindicated below 50 kg body weight and at CrCl below 30 mL/min; protamine does not reverse it.

tiers.label: Any dose
tiers.holdText: ASRA suggests against neuraxial techniques while on a parenteral direct thrombin inhibitor (effect 1–3 h after an IV dose, aPTT-monitored, no reversal agent)
tiers.catheter: Not recommended
tiers.restartText: Not specified

tiers.label: Any dose
tiers.holdText: At least 48 h, with normal clotting studies including fibrinogen; ask about any dural puncture, spinal or epidural in the previous 10 days
tiers.catheter: If given unexpectedly with a catheter in place: limit the infusion to solutions that minimize sensory and motor block; neurologic checks about every 2 h for at least 48 h after the last dose and after removal; removal timing guided by fibrinogen
tiers.restartText: Labeling: no thrombolytics within 10 days of a non-compressible vessel puncture

tiers.label: Any dose
tiers.holdText: No hold: no added risk on their own
tiers.catheter: May stay; caution only with other anticoagulants or coagulopathy
tiers.restartText: No restriction

drugs.name: Clopidogrel

tiers.label: Any dose
tiers.catheter: May stay 1–2 days provided no loading dose is given
tiers.restartText: Resume immediately; 6 h after removal if a loading dose is given

notes: Patients at high bleeding risk need the longer end of the range: about 90% recover platelet function by day 6–7.

drugs.name: Prasugrel

tiers.label: Any dose
tiers.catheter: Do not maintain
tiers.restartText: Resume immediately; 6 h after removal if a loading dose is given

notes: Patients at high bleeding risk need the longer end of the range: about 90% recover platelet function by day 9.

tiers.label: Any dose
tiers.catheter: Do not maintain (rapid onset)
tiers.restartText: Resume immediately; 6 h after removal if a loading dose is given

tiers.label: Infusion
tiers.catheter: Remove before restarting
tiers.restartText: First dose 8 h after catheter removal

drugs.name: GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors

tiers.label: Abciximab
tiers.catheter: If started with a catheter in place: dilute solutions and careful neurologic monitoring
tiers.restartText: Labeling contraindicates use within 4 weeks of surgery

tiers.label: Eptifibatide or tirofiban
tiers.catheter: If started with a catheter in place: dilute solutions and careful neurologic monitoring
tiers.restartText: Labeling contraindicates use within 4 weeks of surgery

notes: Caution with dual therapy: a residual NSAID or aspirin effect adds to the GP IIb/IIIa effect.

tiers.label: Any dose
tiers.catheter: Remove before restarting
tiers.restartText: First dose 6 h after catheter removal

drugs.name: Herbal agents (garlic, ginkgo, ginseng)

tiers.label: Any
tiers.catheter: No restriction alone
tiers.restartText: No restriction

notes: Time to normal hemostasis after stopping: garlic 7 days, ginkgo 36 h, ginseng 24 h; stopping them is not deemed necessary, but combination with anticoagulants or heparin may add risk.

infusions.note: Label figures are the FDA prescribing information as read on DailyMed; off-label regimens name their trial or guideline. Norepinephrine, epinephrine and phenylephrine lead with the usual operating-room start in mcg/min (the label's figures follow); enter a weight for the per-kilogram equivalent. Transfusion thresholds: AABB 2023 (red cells), AABB/ICTMG 2025 (platelets), ASA 2015 and the European trauma guideline 2023 (plasma, cryoprecipitate).

drugs.name: Angiotensin II (Giapreza)
drugs.titration: Up to 15 ng/kg/min every 5 min to the target MAP; wean by up to 15 ng/kg/min every 5–15 min
drugs.range: Maintenance 1.25–40 ng/kg/min
drugs.max: 80 ng/kg/min in the first 3 h; maintenance not above 40 ng/kg/min
drugs.preparation: Dilute in 0.9% saline to 5,000 or 10,000 ng/mL; central line recommended; discard after 24 h
drugs.caution: Thrombosis (13% vs 5% with placebo): give VTE prophylaxis
drugs.source: Giapreza DailyMed prescribing information, La Jolla, rev 12/2021

drugs.name: Norepinephrine (Levophed)
drugs.titration: To the target pressure, checking BP every 2 min until there, then every 5 min; taper on stopping
drugs.range: 4–8 mcg/min is the usual operating-room start (editor's practice). Label: initial 8–12 mcg/min in shock, maintenance 2–4 mcg/min (target systolic 80–100, higher if previously hypertensive); reviews: 0.01–0.3 mcg/kg/min, up to 1 mcg/kg/min in shock
drugs.max: No maximum in the label
drugs.preparation: Label: 4 mg in 1,000 mL D5W or D5/saline = 4 mcg/mL (not saline alone); more concentrated when fluid-restricted; large vein, not the leg veins of the elderly; light-protected, 24 h
drugs.caution: Extravasation (phentolamine infiltration); hypotension if stopped abruptly; arrhythmias; sulfite
drugs.source: Levophed DailyMed prescribing information, Hospira, rev 6/2023; Shankar A et al, Clin Med Insights Cardiol 2022;16; starting range: editor's practice

drugs.name: Phenylephrine
drugs.use: Hypotension during anesthesia, with a normal or fast heart rate
drugs.titration: Infusion to the pressure goal; boluses every 1–2 min as needed
drugs.range: Bolus 40–100 mcg; infusion 10–35 mcg/min
drugs.max: Infusion 200 mcg/min; Biorphen label: boluses up to 200 mcg every 1–2 min
drugs.bolus: 40–100 mcg IV
drugs.preparation: Biorphen 100 mcg/mL ready to use. 10 mg/mL: 1 mL in 99 mL = 100 mcg/mL for boluses; 1 mL in 500 mL = 20 mcg/mL for infusion
drugs.caution: Reflex bradycardia; worsens angina, heart failure and pulmonary hypertension; peripheral and visceral ischemia; extravasation necrosis; weaker in acidosis and hypovolemia
drugs.source: Phenylephrine HCl 10 mg/mL DailyMed prescribing information, Fresenius Kabi, rev 8/2022; Biorphen DailyMed prescribing information, Dr. Reddy's, rev 2/2026

drugs.name: Vasopressin (Vasostrict)
drugs.use: Vasodilatory shock after cardiotomy or sepsis, added to catecholamines
drugs.titration: Up by 0.005 units/min every 10–15 min to the target; after 8 h at target without catecholamines, down by 0.005 units/min every hour
drugs.range: Post-cardiotomy 0.03–0.1 units/min; septic shock start 0.01, range 0.01–0.07 units/min
drugs.max: Limited data above 0.1 units/min (post-cardiotomy) or 0.07 (septic)
drugs.preparation: 20 units/mL vial diluted to 0.1 units/mL (1 unit/mL if fluid-restricted) in saline or D5W; premixed 20, 40 or 60 units/100 mL need no dilution; 18 h at room temperature
drugs.caution: Worsening cardiac function; reversible diabetes insipidus after it stops; not weight-based
drugs.source: Vasostrict DailyMed prescribing information, Par, rev 2/2023

drugs.name: Dobutamine
drugs.use: Low cardiac output with adequate pressure; stress testing
drugs.titration: To heart rate, ectopy, pressure, urine output and cardiac output when measured
drugs.range: 2.5–15 mcg/kg/min raises cardiac output in most patients
drugs.max: Up to 40 mcg/kg/min on rare occasions
drugs.preparation: 250 mg/20 mL; 250 mg in 250 mL = 1,000 mcg/mL (250–5,000 mcg/mL used); not in alkaline solutions; 24 h
drugs.caution: Contraindicated in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy; fast ventricular response in atrial fibrillation; ectopy; correct hypovolemia first; sulfite
drugs.source: Dobutamine injection concentrate DailyMed prescribing information, Hospira, rev 11/2020 (current 5/2026)

drugs.name: Dopamine
drugs.use: Hypotension with low cardiac output; the dose selects the receptor
drugs.titration: Increments of 5–10 mcg/kg/min to effect
drugs.range: Under 5 mcg/kg/min dopaminergic vasodilation; 5–10 β1 (rate and contractility); above 10 α1 vasoconstriction
drugs.max: 50 mcg/kg/min
drugs.preparation: 200–1,600 mcg/mL in 250–1,000 mL; mL/h = dose × kg × 60 ÷ concentration (mcg/mL)
drugs.caution: Extravasation necrosis (phentolamine 5–10 mg in 10–15 mL saline into the area); arrhythmias; hypotension if stopped abruptly; sulfite
drugs.source: Dopamine HCl injection DailyMed prescribing information, Hospira, rev 9/2023

drugs.name: Epinephrine
drugs.use: Low cardiac output or hypotension: inotrope at low rates, pressor at higher
drugs.titration: Label (septic shock): increments of 0.05–0.2 mcg/kg/min every 10–15 min to the target MAP; as an inotrope, titrate to cardiac output and rhythm; wean gradually
drugs.range: 2–4 mcg/min is the usual operating-room start (editor's practice). Cardiogenic shock: 0.01–0.3 mcg/kg/min (Shankar 2022); above that mainly a pressor. Label, septic shock: 0.05–2 mcg/kg/min
drugs.max: 2 mcg/kg/min, the top of the labeled range
drugs.bolus: None by vein in the label (anaphylaxis: 0.3–0.5 mg IM, repeated every 5–10 min)
drugs.preparation: Label: 1 mg in 1,000 mL D5W or D5/saline = 1 mcg/mL (not saline alone); more concentrated solutions by institutional protocol
drugs.caution: Tachyarrhythmia and ischemia; lactate and glucose rise (β2) even at inotropic doses; hypertension and pulmonary edema; extravasation necrosis; sulfite. Inotropic use after bypass is outside the labeled indication
drugs.source: Adrenalin (epinephrine) 1 mg/mL DailyMed prescribing information, Par, rev 6/2026; Shankar A et al, Clin Med Insights Cardiol 2022;16:11795468221075064; starting range: editor's practice

drugs.name: Isoproterenol
drugs.use: Bradycardia or block awaiting pacing, bronchospasm, heart-transplant chronotropy
drugs.titration: To response; if the heart rate passes 110/min consider reducing or pausing
drugs.range: 0.5–5 mcg/min (label, shock); the older 2–10 mcg/min figure for heart block is no longer in current labels or the AHA bradycardia algorithm
drugs.max: 5 mcg/min, the top of the labeled range
drugs.bolus: Bronchospasm during anesthesia: 10–20 mcg IV, repeated
drugs.preparation: 0.2 mg/mL; 1 mg in 500 mL D5W = 2 mcg/mL; bolus 0.2 mg diluted to 10 mL = 20 mcg/mL
drugs.caution: Contraindicated with tachycardia, ventricular arrhythmias and angina; pure β: vasodilation lowers diastolic pressure; sulfite
drugs.source: Isoproterenol HCl injection DailyMed prescribing information, Nexus, rev 3/2023 (Amneal label rev 2/2023 agrees)

drugs.name: Levosimendan (Simdax)
drugs.use: Low-output heart failure; calcium sensitizer (not FDA-approved)
drugs.titration: Down to 0.05 mcg/kg/min or stop for hypotension or tachycardia; up to 0.2 if tolerated and more effect is needed; 24 h infusion, effects last up to 9 days
drugs.range: 0.05–0.2 mcg/kg/min
drugs.max: 0.2 mcg/kg/min
drugs.bolus: Loading 6–12 mcg/kg over 10 min (6 when on other vasodilators or inotropes); often omitted when the pressure is marginal
drugs.preparation: 2.5 mg/mL concentrate: 5 or 10 mL in 500 mL 5% glucose = 0.025 or 0.05 mg/mL (no more concentrated); 24 h
drugs.caution: Not approved in the United States (European SmPC); hypotension and tachycardia; watch ECG, pressure and urine output for 3 days after (5 in renal or hepatic impairment); cardiac-surgery use is off-label even in Europe
drugs.source: Simdax 2.5 mg/mL SmPC (English), Swedish Medical Products Agency, revised 18 Aug 2025

drugs.name: Milrinone
drugs.use: Low cardiac output, pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular failure; inodilator
drugs.titration: 0.375 (minimum), 0.5 (standard) or 0.75 mcg/kg/min; renal adjustment by CrCl: 50 → 0.43, 40 → 0.38, 30 → 0.33, 20 → 0.28, 10 → 0.23, 5 → 0.2 mcg/kg/min
drugs.range: 0.375–0.75 mcg/kg/min
drugs.max: 0.75 mcg/kg/min; 1.13 mg/kg a day
drugs.bolus: Loading 50 mcg/kg over 10 min (label; frequently omitted or given on bypass to avoid the hypotension)
drugs.preparation: 1 mg/mL vials; dilute to 200 mcg/mL in saline or D5W (10 mL + 40 mL); infusions beyond 48 h not studied
drugs.caution: Ventricular arrhythmias; hypotension, more above 0.5 mcg/kg/min; long half-life, longer in renal failure; obstructive valve disease
drugs.source: Milrinone lactate injection DailyMed prescribing information, Hospira, rev 2/2021 (current 10/2025)

drugs.name: Clevidipine (Cleviprex)
drugs.use: Hypertension needing a fast, titratable arterial dilator
drugs.titration: Double the dose every 90 s at first; as the pressure approaches goal, smaller steps every 5–10 min
drugs.range: Most patients respond at 4–6 mg/h; most received 16 mg/h or less
drugs.max: 32 mg/h (limited experience); no more than 1,000 mL (about 21 mg/h) per 24 h because of the lipid load
drugs.preparation: 0.5 mg/mL lipid emulsion, 50 and 100 mL vials; do not dilute; use within 12 h of puncturing the stopper
drugs.caution: Contraindicated with soy or egg allergy, lipid metabolism disorders and severe aortic stenosis; reflex tachycardia; rebound hypertension when stopped; counts toward lipid intake
drugs.source: Cleviprex DailyMed prescribing information, Chiesi, rev 9/2022 (current 11/2025)

drugs.name: Esmolol (Brevibloc)
drugs.use: Tachycardia or hypertension during and after surgery; SVT
drugs.titration: Gradual control: optional repeat 500 mcg/kg load, then infusion up in 50 mcg/kg/min steps every 4 min to 200; once controlled, halve the dose 30 min after the first dose of a longer-acting agent
drugs.range: 50–200 mcg/kg/min for tachycardia; 250–300 may be needed for hypertension
drugs.max: Above 200 mcg/kg/min not recommended for tachycardia; 300 for hypertension (not studied beyond)
drugs.bolus: Immediate control: 1 mg/kg over 30 s, then 150 mcg/kg/min. Gradual control: 500 mcg/kg over 1 min, then 50 mcg/kg/min for 4 min
drugs.preparation: Premixed 10 mg/mL (2,500 mg/250 mL) or 20 mg/mL; 100 mg/10 mL vial; ready to use
drugs.caution: Contraindicated in severe sinus bradycardia, block above first degree, sick sinus, decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic shock, pulmonary hypertension and with IV calcium-channel blockers close in time; hypotension, bronchospasm, hyperkalemia, infusion-site reactions
drugs.source: Brevibloc DailyMed prescribing information, Baxter, rev 3/2025

drugs.name: Nicardipine (Cardene IV)
drugs.use: Hypertension; arterial dilator without negative inotropy
drugs.titration: Up by 2.5 mg/h every 15 min (every 5 min for a rapid reduction); once at goal after rapid titration, down to 3 mg/h; if hypotension or tachycardia, stop and restart at 3–5 mg/h
drugs.max: 15 mg/h
drugs.preparation: Premixed 20 mg/200 mL (0.1 mg/mL: 5 mg/h = 50 mL/h) or 40 mg/200 mL (0.2 mg/mL: 25 mL/h); central line or large peripheral vein, changed every 12 h
drugs.caution: Worsens angina and heart failure; stronger in hepatic impairment, longer in renal impairment; phlebitis
drugs.source: Cardene IV premixed DailyMed prescribing information, Baxter, rev 4/2026

drugs.name: Nitroglycerin
drugs.use: Myocardial ischemia, hypertension with high filling pressures; venodilator
drugs.titration: Up by 5 mcg/min every 3–5 min; if no response at 20 mcg/min, steps of 10–20 mcg/min; smaller steps once a response appears
drugs.range: Wide: some patients need ten to a hundred times the starting dose
drugs.max: No fixed maximum in the label
drugs.preparation: Premixed 25, 50 or 100 mg in 250 mL glass (100, 200 or 400 mcg/mL); PVC tubing adsorbs the drug, so use non-adsorptive sets and no adsorptive in-line filters
drugs.caution: Severe hypotension even at small doses, especially with hypovolemia; paradoxical bradycardia; contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors and riociguat, tamponade, constrictive or restrictive disease and raised ICP; tolerance; methemoglobinemia at high doses
drugs.source: Nitroglycerin in 5% dextrose DailyMed prescribing information, Baxter, rev 8/2016 (current 4/2026)

drugs.name: Nitroprusside
drugs.use: Hypertensive emergency, controlled hypotension, acute afterload reduction
drugs.titration: Small steps every few minutes, waiting at least 5 min before each change; only with continuous arterial pressure
drugs.range: Usual 0.5–10 mcg/kg/min
drugs.max: 10 mcg/kg/min, and never for more than 10 min at that rate; eGFR below 30: average under 3 mcg/kg/min; anuric: 1 mcg/kg/min
drugs.preparation: 50 mg in 250–1,000 mL D5W = 200–50 mcg/mL, wrapped from light, by pump; Nipride RTU 0.5 mg/mL ready to use; discard after 24 h
drugs.caution: Boxed warnings: must be diluted and infused slowly; precipitous hypotension; cyanide toxicity (dose-related, lethal: watch acid-base and venous oxygen) and thiocyanate in renal impairment; never by direct injection; discolored solution is unusable
drugs.source: Sodium nitroprusside 50 mg/2 mL DailyMed prescribing information, Mylan, rev 4/2026; Nipride RTU label, Exela, 2017

drugs.name: Epoprostenol, inhaled
drugs.use: Pulmonary hypertension or right ventricular failure, hypoxemia (off-label by this route)
drugs.titration: Wean by 10 ng/kg/min as tolerated, or halve every 2 h to below 10 then off; protocols start 20–50 ng/kg/min
drugs.range: 5–50 ng/kg/min of ideal body weight; fixed-dose alternative 20 ng/mL at 8–12 mL/h in trials
drugs.max: 50 ng/kg/min; higher doses add nothing
drugs.preparation: Pharmacy-prepared solution in sterile water run by continuous nebulizer in the inspiratory limb
drugs.caution: Off-label route (no FDA inhaled dosing); half-life 3–5 min, so an interrupted circuit means rebound pulmonary hypertension; some systemic hypotension; dose by ideal body weight; filter changes per protocol
drugs.source: Li J et al, J Clin Med 2020;9:464; Benedetto M et al, J Clin Med 2024;13:564; WellSpan Health inhaled epoprostenol protocol

drugs.name: Nitric oxide, inhaled (INOmax)
drugs.use: Pulmonary hypertension or right ventricular failure in adults (off-label; labeled for neonates)
drugs.titration: Wean in steps, pausing hours at each to watch for hypoxemia; never stop abruptly
drugs.range: Adult cardiothoracic use 5–40 ppm; the full pulmonary effect is reached by about 10 ppm
drugs.max: Label: above 20 ppm not recommended; adult trials to 40 ppm
drugs.preparation: 800 or 4,880 ppm cylinders through an approved delivery system with inspired NO₂ and methemoglobin monitoring (MetHb at 4–8 h, then periodically)
drugs.caution: Rebound pulmonary hypertension on withdrawal; methemoglobinemia; NO₂ airway injury; can worsen pulmonary edema with left ventricular failure
drugs.source: INOmax DailyMed prescribing information, INO Therapeutics, rev 4/2023; Benedetto M et al, J Clin Med 2024;13:564

drugs.name: Calcium chloride
drugs.use: Hypotension coming off bypass (off-label); citrate hypocalcemia during massive transfusion
drugs.titration: Off bypass: one bolus over several seconds (ICARUS used 15 mg/kg at the start of weaning; some protocols add 1.5 mg/kg/min for 10 min). Massive transfusion: 1 g after the first unit, then 1 g after every four units, keeping ionized calcium above 1.2 mmol/L (JTS); monitor and correct ionized calcium (European trauma guideline, 1C)
drugs.range: 5–15 mg/kg of calcium chloride appears safe (low-quality evidence)
drugs.max: 15 mg/kg per bolus in the trial; no established maximum
drugs.preparation: 10% calcium chloride = 100 mg/mL (27 mg or 1.4 mmol of elemental calcium per mL); central or large-bore vein
drugs.caution: Transient rise in cardiac index and pressure; theoretical reperfusion injury (the ICARUS question); calcium gluconate for a peripheral line (3 g ≈ 1 g chloride in elemental calcium)
drugs.source: Lomivorotov V et al, ICARUS trial rationale and design, Contemp Clin Trials Commun 2021;23:100835; Joint Trauma System, Damage Control Resuscitation CPG quick reference, June 2023; Rossaint R et al, Crit Care 2023;27:80 (R31)

drugs.name: Diltiazem
drugs.use: Rate control in atrial fibrillation or flutter, SVT
drugs.titration: Second bolus 0.35 mg/kg after 15 min if needed; infusion 10 mg/h (may start at 5), up by 5 mg/h
drugs.range: Infusion 5–15 mg/h, up to 24 h
drugs.max: 15 mg/h
drugs.bolus: 0.25 mg/kg actual weight over 2 min (about 20 mg), then 0.35 mg/kg (about 25 mg)
drugs.preparation: 5 mg/mL; 125 mg in 100 mL = 1 mg/mL; 250 mg in 250 mL = 0.83 mg/mL
drugs.caution: Contraindicated in sick sinus or second- and third-degree block without a pacemaker, cardiogenic shock, IV β-blockers close in time, pre-excited AF (WPW) and ventricular tachycardia; hypotension; heart failure
drugs.source: Diltiazem HCl injection DailyMed prescribing information, Hospira, current 5/2026

drugs.name: Ephedrine
drugs.titration: Repeat boluses to the pressure goal; tachyphylaxis with repeated doses
drugs.max: 50 mg total
drugs.bolus: 5–10 mg IV
drugs.preparation: 50 mg/mL vial: 1 mL + 9 mL saline or D5W = 5 mg/mL; the 5 mg/mL prefilled syringe is not diluted
drugs.caution: Pressor effect with oxytocics; hypertension when given prophylactically; have another pressor ready when it stops working
drugs.source: Akovaz (ephedrine sulfate) DailyMed prescribing information, Exela, rev 11/2020

drugs.name: Hydralazine
drugs.use: Hypertension when a slower, longer arteriolar dilator is wanted
drugs.titration: Repeat as necessary; the pressure falls within minutes and bottoms at 10–80 min, so wait before redosing; lower doses with renal damage
drugs.max: No maximum in the label
drugs.bolus: 20–40 mg IV or IM (the label's dose; many anesthesiologists give smaller increments)
drugs.preparation: 20 mg/mL, 1 mL vial; give at once, do not add to infusion fluids; discard if discolored
drugs.caution: Contraindicated in coronary artery disease and mitral valvular rheumatic heart disease; reflex tachycardia; worsens cerebral ischemia with raised ICP; lupus-like syndrome with chronic use
drugs.source: Hydralazine HCl injection DailyMed prescribing information, Fresenius Kabi, rev 10/2025

drugs.name: Hydroxocobalamin (Cyanokit)
drugs.use: Vasoplegia after bypass (off-label; labeled for cyanide poisoning)
drugs.titration: A second 5 g may follow, over 15 min to 2 h depending on the response
drugs.max: 10 g in total
drugs.bolus: 5 g over 15 min
drugs.preparation: 5 g vial + 200 mL 0.9% saline = 25 mg/mL; rock for 60 s, do not shake
drugs.caution: Hypertension; anaphylaxis; oxalate kidney injury (check renal function for a week); red plasma and urine interfere with colorimetric labs and trip dialysis blood-leak alarms; case series only for vasoplegia
drugs.source: Cyanokit DailyMed prescribing information, BTG, rev 5/2021; Busse LW et al, Crit Care 2020;24:36; Unic-Stojanovic D et al, Interdiscip Cardiovasc Thorac Surg 2025;40(4):ivaf075

drugs.name: Labetalol
drugs.titration: 40 mg, then 80 mg at 10-min intervals to the target, or an infusion at 2 mg/min
drugs.range: Usual cumulative dose 50–200 mg
drugs.max: 300 mg in total
drugs.bolus: 20 mg over 2 min, then 40–80 mg every 10 min
drugs.preparation: 5 mg/mL; infusion 200 mg in 160 mL = 1 mg/mL at 2 mL/min; keep the patient supine
drugs.caution: Contraindicated in asthma, overt heart failure, block above first degree, cardiogenic shock and severe bradycardia; orthostatic hypotension for hours; hepatic injury
drugs.source: Labetalol HCl injection DailyMed prescribing information, Hospira, rev 11/2022 (current 7/2026)

drugs.name: Methylene blue (ProvayBlue)
drugs.use: Vasoplegia after bypass (off-label; labeled for methemoglobinemia)
drugs.titration: Vasoplegia reports: 1–2 mg/kg over 15–30 min, some followed by 0.25–2 mg/kg/h; label (methemoglobinemia): 1 mg/kg over 5–30 min, repeated once after an hour if needed
drugs.max: Label: two doses; eGFR 15–59: a single 1 mg/kg. Adverse effects reported above 2 mg/kg
drugs.bolus: 1–2 mg/kg over 15–30 min
drugs.preparation: 5 mg/mL; may be diluted in 50 mL D5W, not saline (solubility)
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs (and opioids such as fentanyl, meperidine, tramadol, methadone); contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (hemolysis); falsely low pulse oximetry and BIS readings; blue-green skin and urine
drugs.source: ProvayBlue DailyMed prescribing information, American Regent, rev 2/2024; Busse LW et al, Crit Care 2020;24:36; Unic-Stojanovic D et al, 2025

drugs.name: Phenylephrine
drugs.use: Bolus for hypotension during anesthesia, with a normal or fast heart rate
drugs.titration: Repeat every 1–2 min as needed; start an infusion when boluses keep coming
drugs.max: Biorphen label: boluses up to 200 mcg every 1–2 min; Fresenius label: total bolus dosage not above 200 mcg
drugs.bolus: 40–100 mcg IV
drugs.preparation: Biorphen 100 mcg/mL ready to use. 10 mg/mL: 1 mL in 99 mL saline or D5W = 100 mcg/mL
drugs.caution: Reflex bradycardia; worsens angina, heart failure and pulmonary hypertension; weaker in acidosis and hypovolemia
drugs.source: Phenylephrine HCl 10 mg/mL DailyMed prescribing information, Fresenius Kabi, rev 8/2022; Biorphen DailyMed prescribing information, Dr. Reddy's, rev 2/2026

drugs.name: Amiodarone (Nexterone)
drugs.use: Ventricular arrhythmias; rate and rhythm control in atrial fibrillation
drugs.titration: 150 mg over 10 min (15 mg/min), then 1 mg/min for 6 h (360 mg), then 0.5 mg/min (540 mg over the next 18 h; 720 mg per 24 h thereafter); repeat 150 mg over 10 min for breakthrough VF or unstable VT
drugs.range: Cardiac arrest, VF or pulseless VT: 300 mg IV push, then 150 mg (AHA ACLS 2020)
drugs.max: Concentrations above 3 mg/mL cause phlebitis: a dedicated central line whenever possible
drugs.bolus: 150 mg over 10 min
drugs.preparation: Premixed in dextrose: 150 mg/100 mL (1.5 mg/mL) and 360 mg/200 mL (1.8 mg/mL), no dilution
drugs.caution: Hypotension (slow the infusion; pressors or volume); bradycardia and AV block (slow or stop; pacing available); QTc prolongation and torsades; hepatic and pulmonary injury with continued use
drugs.source: Nexterone (amiodarone) premixed injection DailyMed prescribing information, Baxter, rev 4/2024; AHA 2020 adult cardiac arrest algorithm

drugs.name: Dexmedetomidine (Precedex)
drugs.use: Sedation without respiratory depression; opioid-sparing adjunct
drugs.titration: Procedural sedation: start 0.6 mcg/kg/h, 0.2–1 mcg/kg/h; 0.7 mcg/kg/h until the tube is secured for awake fiberoptic intubation; ICU sedation 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/h
drugs.range: 0.2–1 mcg/kg/h
drugs.max: Beyond 24 h: tolerance, tachyphylaxis and more adverse effects
drugs.bolus: Load 1 mcg/kg over 10 min (0.5 mcg/kg over 65 or for less invasive procedures); often omitted, and not needed when converting from another sedative
drugs.preparation: Premixed 4 mcg/mL (200 mcg/50 mL, 400 mcg/100 mL)
drugs.caution: Bradycardia and hypotension, some fatal, worse with hypovolemia, diabetes, chronic hypertension and age; transient hypertension during the load (slow it); reduce the dose in the elderly and in hepatic impairment; patients are arousable, which is not failure
drugs.source: Dexmedetomidine in 0.9% sodium chloride DailyMed prescribing information, Baxter, rev 12/2025

drugs.name: Insulin, regular, IV
drugs.use: Hyperglycemia during and after cardiac surgery
drugs.range: By institutional protocol (commonly 1–2 units/h to start, or 0.02–0.05 units/kg/h, adjusted hourly to the glucose); diabetic ketoacidosis 0.1 units/kg/h. Cardiac surgery: an insulin infusion to keep glucose ≤ 180 mg/dL in the operating room and for at least 24 h after (STS 2009, class I)
drugs.preparation: Regular insulin 100 units/mL diluted to 1 unit/mL in 0.9% saline; prime the tubing
drugs.caution: Hypoglycemia: glucose at least hourly on an infusion; potassium falls with insulin; the target is ≤ 180 mg/dL, not tight control (NICE-SUGAR)
drugs.source: Lazar HL et al, STS practice guideline: blood glucose management during adult cardiac surgery, Ann Thorac Surg 2009;87:663–669; Humulin R prescribing information (IV use under medical supervision); starting rates: institutional practice

drugs.name: Ketamine (Ketalar)
drugs.use: Induction with hemodynamic support; analgesic adjunct at subanesthetic doses
drugs.titration: Label induction 1–4.5 mg/kg IV over 60 s (2 mg/kg gives 5–10 min); maintenance half to the full induction dose as needed, or 0.1–0.5 mg/min by infusion; less when combined with other agents
drugs.range: Analgesic (subanesthetic) use: bolus up to 0.35 mg/kg and infusion up to 1 mg/kg/h without intensive monitoring (ASRA/AAPM/ASA 2018 consensus)
drugs.bolus: 1–2 mg/kg over 60 s; IM 6.5–13 mg/kg
drugs.preparation: 10, 50 and 100 mg/mL; the 100 mg/mL must be diluted for IV use; infusion 1 mg/mL (500 mg in 500 mL), used at once
drugs.caution: Transient hypertension, tachycardia and a rise in cardiac index; intracranial pressure rises; emergence reactions in about 12%, fewer with a benzodiazepine and lower doses; respiratory depression with fast injection; abuse potential
drugs.source: Ketalar DailyMed prescribing information, Par, rev 3/2026; Schwenk ES et al, Reg Anesth Pain Med 2018;43:456–466

drugs.name: Lidocaine, intravenous
drugs.titration: Antiarrhythmic (label): 1–1.5 mg/kg at 25–50 mg/min, then 1–4 mg/min (20–50 mcg/kg/min), halved after 24 h; stop once the rhythm is stable. Analgesic (consensus 2021): no more than 1.5 mg/kg of ideal body weight over 10 min, then up to 1.5 mg/kg/h (ideal weight), for no longer than 24 h
drugs.range: Infusion 1–4 mg/min
drugs.max: Analgesic infusion: 120 mg/h and 24 h; not under 40 kg; CNS toxicity above 6 mcg/mL
drugs.bolus: 1–1.5 mg/kg (label); 1.5 mg/kg of ideal weight over 10 min (analgesic)
drugs.preparation: Premixed 4 and 8 mg/mL in dextrose for the antiarrhythmic infusion; the analgesic bolus is given with ECG, oximetry and an anesthesiologist present
drugs.caution: Neurological symptoms come first (perioral numbness, tinnitus, confusion), cardiac depression late; bradycardia and heart block; no nerve or fascial plane block within 4 h before or after the infusion, and no epidural or wound-catheter bolus for 4 h after; 20% lipid emulsion at hand; additive with other antiarrhythmics; lower rates in hepatic and severe renal impairment
drugs.source: Lidocaine hydrochloride and dextrose injection DailyMed prescribing information, Baxter, rev 2/2026; Foo I et al, international consensus statement on intravenous lidocaine, Anaesthesia 2021;76:238–250

drugs.name: Propofol (Diprivan)
drugs.use: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia; sedation
drugs.titration: Maintenance 100–200 mcg/kg/min in healthy adults, 50–100 in the elderly, debilitated or ASA III–IV, 25–100 for cardiac anesthesia; sedation 25–75 mcg/kg/min after 100–150 for 3–5 min (or 0.5 mg/kg slowly); ICU: start 5 mcg/kg/min, steps of 5–10 every 5 min or more, usual 5–50
drugs.range: Intermittent maintenance boluses 20–50 mg
drugs.max: ICU: not above 4 mg/kg/h (67 mcg/kg/min) unless the benefit outweighs the risk; infusion syndrome with more than 5 mg/kg/h beyond 48 h
drugs.bolus: Induction 2–2.5 mg/kg (healthy, under 65), 1–1.5 mg/kg (elderly, debilitated, ASA III–IV), 0.5–1.5 mg/kg (cardiac anesthesia), 1–2 mg/kg (neurosurgical), given until induction
drugs.preparation: 10 mg/mL emulsion; strict asepsis, one patient per vial, finished within 12 h of opening
drugs.caution: Hypotension, more with hypovolemia and age (about 80% of the adult dose, no fast boluses); infusion syndrome; lipid load and triglycerides on long infusions; pain on injection
drugs.source: Diprivan DailyMed prescribing information, Fresenius Kabi, rev 1/2025

drugs.name: Remifentanil (Ultiva)
drugs.use: Intense, short-acting opioid for anesthesia maintenance and sedation
drugs.titration: Maintenance with propofol or isoflurane 0.25 (0.05–2) mcg/kg/min, with nitrous oxide 0.4 (0.1–2); induction 0.5–1; continued as the postoperative analgesic 0.1 (0.025–0.2); sedation 0.1 then 0.05 (0.025–0.2), halved with midazolam
drugs.range: 0.025–2 mcg/kg/min by phase
drugs.max: Elderly (over 65): halve the starting doses; dose obese patients (over 30% above ideal) on ideal body weight
drugs.bolus: 1 mcg/kg over 30–60 s, optional at induction and as a supplement (0.5 mcg/kg with midazolam for sedation)
drugs.preparation: 20, 25, 50 or 250 mcg/mL (25 for sedation)
drugs.caution: Analgesia is gone 5–10 min after stopping: establish other analgesia before the end; chest-wall rigidity with boluses above 1 mcg/kg or fast rates; respiratory depression in the spontaneously breathing (halve the rate); no bolus for postoperative analgesia
drugs.source: Ultiva DailyMed prescribing information, Mylan, rev 12/2025

drugs.name: Cryoprecipitate
drugs.titration: Repeat by fibrinogen level or viscoelastic testing
drugs.range: 1 unit per 7–10 kg raises fibrinogen by about 50–75 mg/dL; trauma: 15–20 single-donor units (about 3–4 g fibrinogen) to start; cardiac surgery: 10 units (about 4 g, FIBRES). Indications: excessive bleeding with fibrinogen < 80–100 mg/dL (ASA 2015); trauma: ≤ 1.5 g/L (150 mg/dL) or viscoelastic signs of a functional deficit (European 2023)
drugs.preparation: Pooled (5 or 10 units), thawed; each unit at least 150 mg fibrinogen and 80 units factor VIII
drugs.caution: Recovery of transfused fibrinogen is 50–60%; ABO-compatible preferred; fibrinogen concentrate is an alternative (see Factor Concentrates)
drugs.source: ASA Task Force on Perioperative Blood Management, Practice guidelines for perioperative blood management, Anesthesiology 2015;122:241–275; Circular of Information for the Use of Human Blood and Blood Components (AABB/ARC/ABC/ASBP); Rossaint R et al, Crit Care 2023;27:80 (R29); Callum J et al, FIBRES, JAMA 2019
drugs.threshold: Bleeding with fibrinogen < 80–100 mg/dL · trauma ≤ 150 mg/dL (1.5 g/L)

drugs.name: Plasma (FFP, thawed plasma)
drugs.use: Coagulopathy with bleeding; urgent warfarin reversal when PCC is not available
drugs.titration: Further plasma by PT/aPTT or viscoelastic testing (1C); not for hypofibrinogenemia on its own (1C)
drugs.range: Standard dose about 15 mL/kg (Circular); cardiac surgery comparator in FARES-II: 3 units ≤ 60 kg, 4 units > 60 kg; trauma: plasma to red cells at least 1:2. Indications: excessive microvascular bleeding with INR > 2.0 in the absence of heparin (ASA 2015); trauma: PT or aPTT > 1.5× normal (European 2023)
drugs.preparation: Thawed, ABO-compatible
drugs.caution: Volume overload (TACO) and TRALI; in cardiac surgery coagulopathy, prothrombin complex concentrate gave hemostasis more often (77.9% vs 60.4%, FARES-II)
drugs.source: ASA Task Force on Perioperative Blood Management, Practice guidelines for perioperative blood management, Anesthesiology 2015;122:241–275; Circular of Information for the Use of Human Blood and Blood Components (AABB/ARC/ABC/ASBP); Karkouti K et al, FARES-II, JAMA 2025;333:1781–1792; Rossaint R et al, Crit Care 2023;27:80 (R25, R27)
drugs.threshold: Bleeding with INR > 2.0 (no heparin) · trauma: PT or aPTT > 1.5× normal

drugs.name: Platelets
drugs.use: Thrombocytopenia or platelet dysfunction with bleeding, or before a procedure
drugs.titration: Keep above 50 × 10⁹/L while bleeding, above 100 with traumatic brain injury (European 2023, 2C); a high platelet-to-red-cell ratio in massive transfusion (2B)
drugs.range: Thresholds (AABB/ICTMG 2025): major non-neuraxial surgery < 50 × 10⁹/L; interventional radiology < 20 (low risk) or < 50 (high risk); lumbar puncture < 20; central line at a compressible site < 10; prophylaxis in hypoproliferative thrombocytopenia < 10; not for cardiac surgery without thrombocytopenia or major bleeding. Bleeding surgical patients: usually indicated below 50, rarely above 100 (ASA 2015)
drugs.preparation: One apheresis unit (at least 3 × 10¹¹) ≈ 6 whole-blood-derived units; 4–8 single units or one apheresis pack to start in trauma; children 5–10 mL/kg or 1 unit per 10 kg; apheresis unit 250–300 mL
drugs.caution: Transfusion reactions, bacterial contamination (stored warm) and TRALI; antiplatelet drugs inactivate transfused platelets while still circulating
drugs.source: Metcalf RA et al, Platelet transfusion: 2025 AABB and ICTMG international clinical practice guidelines, JAMA 2025;334(7), doi:10.1001/jama.2025.7529; ASA Task Force on Perioperative Blood Management, Practice guidelines for perioperative blood management, Anesthesiology 2015;122:241–275; Rossaint R et al, Crit Care 2023;27:80 (R30); Circular of Information for the Use of Human Blood and Blood Components (AABB/ARC/ABC/ASBP)
drugs.threshold: < 50 × 10⁹/L bleeding or major surgery · < 20 lumbar puncture · < 10 prophylaxis or central line

drugs.name: Red blood cells
drugs.use: Anemia or blood loss with inadequate oxygen delivery
drugs.titration: Adults: one unit at a time, reassessing between units (ASA 2015). Children: 10–15 mL/kg of additive-solution red cells (Circular)
drugs.range: Restrictive thresholds (AABB 2023): Hb < 7 g/dL for hospitalized adults, including critically ill and hematology-oncology patients; 7.5 g/dL in cardiac surgery; 8 g/dL in orthopedic surgery or preexisting cardiovascular disease. Rarely needed above 10 g/dL; between 6 and 10, decide on bleeding, volume, organ ischemia and reserve (ASA 2015). Children: < 7 g/dL when critically ill; congenital heart disease 7 g/dL (biventricular repair), 9 g/dL (single-ventricle palliation), 7–9 g/dL (uncorrected)
drugs.preparation: About 300–400 mL per additive-solution unit; one unit raises Hb by about 1 g/dL (hematocrit by 3%) in an average-sized adult
drugs.caution: Not for volume expansion or anemia a hematinic can correct; massive transfusion: give plasma and platelets in ratio (trauma, at least 1:2 plasma to red cells) and calcium 1 g after the first unit and every four units
drugs.source: Carson JL et al, Red blood cell transfusion: 2023 AABB international guidelines, JAMA 2023;330:1892–1902; ASA Task Force on Perioperative Blood Management, Practice guidelines for perioperative blood management, Anesthesiology 2015;122:241–275; Circular of Information for the Use of Human Blood and Blood Components (AABB/ARC/ABC/ASBP)
drugs.threshold: Hb < 7 g/dL · 7.5 cardiac surgery · 8 orthopedic surgery or cardiovascular disease

drugs.name: Antithrombin III (Thrombate III)
drugs.use: Heparin resistance before bypass (off-label); hereditary deficiency
drugs.range: Heparin resistance: 500–1,000 units, or 75 units/kg; 1 unit/kg raises activity about 1.4%. Label (hereditary deficiency): units = (120 − baseline %) × kg ÷ 1.4, then 60% of that about every 24 h to keep 80–120%
drugs.max: None stated; infuse over 10–20 min
drugs.preparation: About 500 units per vial + 10 mL sterile water = 50 units/mL; use within 3 h
drugs.caution: Heparin resistance is usually an ACT under 480 s after 400–450 units/kg; antithrombin concentrate reduces plasma transfusion for it (STS/SCA/AmSECT/SABM 2021 class I, A) but is not for bleeding (EACTS/EACTA 2017 class III); heparin effect then increases
drugs.source: Thrombate III DailyMed prescribing information, Grifols, rev 7/2025; Beattie GW, Jeffrey RR, Interact Cardiovasc Thorac Surg 2013;18:117–120; Tibi P et al, 2021; Pagano D et al, Eur J Cardiothorac Surg 2018;53:79–111

drugs.name: Factor IX concentrate (BeneFIX)
drugs.range: Units = kg × desired rise (IU/dL) × 1.3 (12 y and over; 1.4 under 12): recovery about 0.8 IU/dL per IU/kg. Minor bleed target 20–30%, moderate 25–50%, major bleed or surgery 50–100%, every 12–24 h for 7–10 days
drugs.preparation: Lyophilized kit with its diluent; slow IV push over minutes; continuous infusion not established
drugs.caution: Inhibitors; anaphylaxis; thromboembolism
drugs.source: BeneFIX DailyMed prescribing information, Pfizer, rev 11/2022 (current 2/2025)

drugs.name: Factor VIIa, recombinant (NovoSeven RT)
drugs.use: Hemophilia with inhibitors; last resort for intractable bleeding after bypass (off-label)
drugs.titration: Label: every 2 h until hemostasis, then every 3–6 h; acquired hemophilia 70–90 mcg/kg; factor VII deficiency 15–30
drugs.range: Cardiac surgery (off-label, Gill 2009 RCT): 40 or 80 mcg/kg once, fewer reoperations for bleeding (14% and 12% vs 25%) but numerically more deaths and strokes; STS/SCA/AmSECT/SABM 2021: may be considered for intractable non-surgical bleeding (IIb, B-NR)
drugs.max: None stated
drugs.bolus: Slow IV over 2–5 min
drugs.preparation: 1, 2, 5 and 8 mg vials with histidine diluent = 1 mg/mL (1,000 mcg/mL); use within 3 h
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: arterial and venous thrombosis; correct platelets, fibrinogen, temperature, pH and calcium first; antibodies in factor VII deficiency
drugs.source: NovoSeven RT DailyMed prescribing information, Novo Nordisk, rev 7/2020; Gill R et al, Circulation 2009;120:21–27; Tibi P et al, 2021

drugs.name: Factor VIII concentrate (Advate)
drugs.range: Units = kg × desired rise (IU/dL) × 0.5: 1 IU/kg raises factor VIII about 2 IU/dL. Minor bleed 20–40% (10–20 IU/kg), major bleed or surgery 80–120% (40–60 IU/kg before, then every 8–24 h)
drugs.max: Infuse at up to 10 mL/min (over 5 min or less)
drugs.preparation: Lyophilized kit with its diluent
drugs.caution: Inhibitors; hypersensitivity
drugs.source: Advate DailyMed prescribing information, Takeda, rev 3/2025

drugs.name: FEIBA (anti-inhibitor coagulant complex)
drugs.use: Hemophilia with inhibitors; bleeding on emicizumab needs care
drugs.titration: Every 6 h (mucous membrane) to 12 h (joint) by bleed type; prophylaxis 85 units/kg every other day
drugs.max: 100 units/kg per dose, 200 units/kg per day; no faster than 10 units/kg/min
drugs.preparation: 500, 1,000 and 2,500-unit vials with 10, 20 or 50 mL sterile water; use within 3 h, not refrigerated after mixing
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: thrombotic events, more above 200 units/kg/day and with rFVIIa or emicizumab; contraindicated in DIC and acute thrombosis or infarction
drugs.source: FEIBA DailyMed prescribing information, Takeda, rev 12/2024 (current 12/2025)

drugs.name: Fibrinogen concentrate (RiaSTAP, Fibryga)
drugs.use: Acquired or congenital hypofibrinogenemia with bleeding
drugs.titration: Dose (mg/kg) = (target − measured mg/dL) ÷ 1.7 (RiaSTAP; 1.8 for Fibryga in adults); 70 mg/kg when the level is unknown. Fibryga for acquired deficiency: adults 4 g fixed, 12–17 y 50 mg/kg, under 12 y 70 mg/kg; repeat if fibrinogen ≤ 200 mg/dL or FIBTEM A10 ≤ 10 mm
drugs.range: 1 mg/kg raises fibrinogen about 1.7–1.8 mg/dL. Cardiac surgery: 4 g, repeated as needed in the first 24 h, non-inferior to 10 units cryoprecipitate (FIBRES); trauma: 3–4 g at Clauss ≤ 1.5 g/L
drugs.max: None stated; infuse at up to 5 mL/min (20 mL/min for Fibryga in acquired deficiency)
drugs.preparation: 1 g + 50 mL sterile water (about 20 mg/mL); 2 g + 100 mL
drugs.caution: Thrombosis; hypersensitivity; not for dysfibrinogenemia
drugs.source: RiaSTAP DailyMed prescribing information, CSL Behring, rev 12/2025; Fibryga DailyMed prescribing information, Octapharma, rev 8/2025; Callum J et al, FIBRES, JAMA 2019; Rossaint R et al, Crit Care 2023;27:80

drugs.name: Prothrombin complex concentrate, 4-factor (Kcentra)
drugs.use: Warfarin reversal; coagulopathic bleeding after bypass (off-label)
drugs.titration: Warfarin reversal by INR: 2 to under 4 → 25 units/kg (max 2,500); 4–6 → 35 (max 3,500); above 6 → 50 (max 5,000), weight capped at 100 kg; give vitamin K with it; no repeat dosing
drugs.range: Cardiac surgery coagulopathy (FARES-II): 1,500 units if ≤ 60 kg, 2,000 units if > 60 kg, one further dose allowed within 24 h; hemostasis in 77.9% vs 60.4% with plasma
drugs.max: 2,500 / 3,500 / 5,000 units by INR band; infuse at 0.12 mL/kg/min (about 3 units/kg/min), at most 8.4 mL/min
drugs.preparation: 500-unit kit + 20 mL, 1,000-unit kit + 40 mL sterile water (20–31 units/mL); the factor IX units are printed on each vial
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: arterial and venous thromboembolism; contraindicated in DIC and HIT (contains heparin); STS/SCA/AmSECT/SABM 2021: reasonable before plasma as first line for refractory coagulopathy (IIa, B-NR)
drugs.source: Kcentra DailyMed prescribing information, CSL Behring, rev 5/2023; Karkouti K et al, FARES-II, JAMA 2025;333:1781–1792; Tibi P et al, 2021

drugs.name: Aminocaproic acid (Amicar)
drugs.use: Antifibrinolytic for cardiac surgery (regimens off-label) and fibrinolytic bleeding
drugs.titration: Label: 4–5 g in 250 mL over the first hour, then 1 g/h for about 8 h or until bleeding is controlled
drugs.range: Cardiac surgery: 10 g load then 2 g/h on bypass (BART); or 100 mg/kg load, 5 mg/kg in the prime, 30 mg/kg/h (Walley 2017)
drugs.max: None in the label; rapid undiluted injection is not recommended (hypotension, bradycardia, arrhythmia)
drugs.bolus: 4–5 g over 1 h (label); 10 g (BART)
drugs.preparation: 250 mg/mL; 4–5 g in 250 mL over an hour, then 1 g in 50 mL each hour
drugs.caution: Antifibrinolytic (EACA or tranexamic acid) reduces blood loss and transfusion in cardiac surgery: STS/SCA/AmSECT/SABM 2021 class I, level A; avoid with DIC or upper urinary tract bleeding
drugs.source: Aminocaproic acid injection USP prescribing information, Pfizer; BART registration ISRCTN15166455; Walley H et al, Glob Cardiol Sci Pract 2017;2017(2):12; Tibi P et al, J Extra Corpor Technol 2021;53:97–124

drugs.name: Desmopressin (DDAVP)
drugs.use: Platelet dysfunction (uremia, aspirin, bypass), mild hemophilia A, von Willebrand type 1
drugs.titration: Over 15–30 min, 30 min before the procedure; for bleeding repeat after 8–12 h, then daily; tachyphylaxis if more often than every 48 h
drugs.max: 20 mcg per dose
drugs.preparation: 4 mcg/mL; dilute in 50 mL 0.9% saline (10 mL below 10 kg)
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: hyponatremia (seizures, coma, death); contraindicated with CrCl under 50, hyponatremia, SIADH, heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, loop diuretics or glucocorticoids; hypotension when given fast; thrombosis in type 2B von Willebrand; cardiac-surgery use off-label (STS/SCA/AmSECT/SABM 2021 class IIb)
drugs.source: DDAVP injection DailyMed prescribing information, Ferring, rev 7/2022; Tibi P et al, 2021

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid
drugs.use: Antifibrinolytic for cardiac surgery and trauma (regimens off-label)
drugs.titration: Cardiac surgery: low regimen 10 mg/kg load, 2 mg/kg/h, 1 mg/kg in the prime; high regimen 30 mg/kg, 16 mg/kg/h, 2 mg/kg in the prime (OPTIMAL trial arms). Trauma (CRASH-2): 1 g over 10 min within 3 h, then 1 g over 8 h
drugs.range: Label (hemophilia, dental extraction): 10 mg/kg before, then 10 mg/kg three to four times daily; renal dosing by creatinine
drugs.max: Infuse no faster than 100 mg/min (hypotension). Seizures are dose-related: 1% with the high regimen vs 0.4% with the low (OPTIMAL)
drugs.bolus: 10–30 mg/kg (cardiac); 1 g over 10 min (trauma)
drugs.preparation: 100 mg/mL (1 g/10 mL); undiluted or diluted to 10–20 mg/mL; compatible with heparin; never mixed with blood or penicillins
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: inadvertent intrathecal injection has been fatal, so keep it away from the neuraxial tray; contraindicated in subarachnoid hemorrhage and active intravascular clotting; thromboembolism; visual disturbance
drugs.source: Cyklokapron DailyMed prescribing information, Pfizer, rev 8/2025; Shi J et al, OPTIMAL, JAMA 2022;328:336–347; CRASH-2 collaborators, Lancet 2010;376:23–32

drugs.name: Bivalirudin
drugs.use: Anticoagulation for bypass or PCI when heparin cannot be used (HIT)
drugs.titration: Bypass in HIT (off-label, STS/SCA/AmSECT 2018): 1 mg/kg bolus, 2.5 mg/kg/h, 50 mg in the prime, ACT target 2.5 × baseline. PCI (label): 0.75 mg/kg bolus then 1.75 mg/kg/h for the procedure, ACT at 5 min and a further 0.3 mg/kg if needed; up to 4 h after PCI in STEMI
drugs.range: Renal: infusion 1 mg/kg/h when CrCl is below 30 mL/min, 0.25 mg/kg/h on hemodialysis; the bolus is not reduced
drugs.bolus: 1 mg/kg (bypass); 0.75 mg/kg (PCI)
drugs.preparation: 250 mg vial + 5 mL sterile water, then diluted to 5 mg/mL
drugs.caution: No reversal agent (half-life about 25 min, longer in renal failure); blood that stands still clots — keep cardiotomy suction, grafts and the circuit flushed and moving; more bleeding with heparin, warfarin, thrombolytics or GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors; thrombosis with gamma brachytherapy; studied with aspirin
drugs.source: Bivalirudin for injection DailyMed prescribing information, Fresenius Kabi, rev 4/2025; Shore-Lesserson L et al, STS/SCA/AmSECT anticoagulation guideline, J Extra Corpor Technol 2018;50:5–18

drugs.name: Heparin for cardiopulmonary bypass
drugs.titration: Clotting time before bypass and at intervals (class I); keep the ACT above 480 s on bypass (IIa; above 400 s on some maximal-activation instruments); redose by ACT, or by heparin concentration (IIb)
drugs.range: Label: at least 150 units/kg, usually 300 (under 60 min) or 400 units/kg (over 60 min); EACTS/EACTA 2017: 300–600 units/kg to an ACT of 300–600 s
drugs.max: More than 400 units/kg invites heparin rebound
drugs.bolus: One weight-based bolus, undiluted or in 50–100 mL saline, before cannulation
drugs.preparation: 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000 units/mL vials: fatal concentration errors are on record
drugs.caution: HIT: bivalirudin is a reasonable alternative (1 mg/kg load, 2.5 mg/kg/h, 50 mg in the prime, to 2.5× baseline ACT, per the 2018 guideline); heparin resistance: see antithrombin
drugs.source: Heparin sodium injection DailyMed prescribing information, Pfizer, rev 9/2025; Shore-Lesserson L et al, STS/SCA/AmSECT anticoagulation guideline, J Extra Corpor Technol 2018;50:5–18; Pagano D et al, 2018

drugs.name: Andexanet alfa (Andexxa)
drugs.use: Reversal of rivaroxaban or apixaban with life-threatening bleeding
drugs.titration: Low dose: 400 mg at 30 mg/min, then 4 mg/min for up to 120 min (480 mg). High dose: 800 mg at 30 mg/min, then 8 mg/min for up to 120 min (960 mg)
drugs.range: Low dose: rivaroxaban ≤ 10 mg or apixaban ≤ 5 mg, and any dose taken 8 h or more earlier. High dose: rivaroxaban > 10 mg or apixaban > 5 mg (or unknown dose) within 8 h or at an unknown time
drugs.max: 960 mg; more than one course not evaluated
drugs.preparation: 200 mg vials + 20 mL sterile water = 10 mg/mL (5 vials low dose, 9 high); swirl, do not shake
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: thromboembolism, ischemic events, cardiac arrest, sudden death. Heparin stops working after it (ACT will not prolong): do not give before heparinization for bypass; use a non-heparin anticoagulant if surgery cannot wait. Not for edoxaban, enoxaparin or betrixaban
drugs.source: Andexxa DailyMed prescribing information, AstraZeneca, rev 5/2025

drugs.name: Idarucizumab (Praxbind)
drugs.use: Reversal of dabigatran for bleeding or emergency surgery
drugs.titration: A second 5 g may be considered if bleeding recurs with prolonged clotting times or a second emergency procedure is needed
drugs.max: 5 g per course; repeat dosing not established
drugs.bolus: Two 2.5 g/50 mL vials, back to back, by infusion or syringe
drugs.preparation: No dilution or mixing; flush with 0.9% saline; use within 6 h of opening
drugs.caution: Thromboembolism (restart dabigatran after 24 h); clotting times may rise again; sorbitol (hereditary fructose intolerance)
drugs.source: Praxbind DailyMed prescribing information, Boehringer Ingelheim, rev 11/2023

drugs.name: Protamine
drugs.titration: By ACT (or heparin titration); for heparin rebound an infusion of 25 mg/h for up to 6 h may be considered (IIb)
drugs.range: 1 mg neutralizes about 100 units of heparin; less is needed as time passes (half the dose may do 30 min after heparin). Society ratios: under 2.6 mg per 100 units given (STS/SCA/AmSECT 2018, IIa), or under 1:1 of the initial bolus (EACTS/EACTA 2017, IIa)
drugs.max: 50 mg in any 10 min, by slow IV injection over 10 min
drugs.preparation: 10 mg/mL (50 mg/5 mL, 250 mg/25 mL); may be diluted in D5W or saline; do not store diluted
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: severe hypotension, cardiovascular collapse, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, catastrophic pulmonary vasoconstriction; risk higher with fast or high doses, repeat exposure, NPH insulin, fish allergy, vasectomy, poor LV function and pulmonary hypertension; ratios above 5:1 impair platelets; heparin rebound 30 min to 18 h later
drugs.source: Protamine sulfate injection DailyMed prescribing information, Fresenius Kabi, rev 11/2024; Shore-Lesserson L et al, 2018; Pagano D et al, 2018

drugs.name: Vitamin K (phytonadione)
drugs.use: Warfarin reversal alongside PCC, when hours are available
drugs.titration: Up to 25–50 mg as one dose; recheck the INR after 6–8 h and repeat if still prolonged; with PCC for urgent reversal, 5–10 mg IV (European trauma guideline, 1A)
drugs.max: 50 mg as a single dose; IV no faster than 1 mg/min
drugs.preparation: 10 mg/mL and 1 mg/0.5 mL; dilute only in saline, D5W or D5/saline; give at once, protected from light
drugs.caution: Boxed warning: fatal anaphylaxis by the IV and IM routes even when diluted and given slowly, so subcutaneous when time allows; aluminum
drugs.source: Vitamin K1 injectable emulsion prescribing information, Hospira/Pfizer, rev 9–10/2025; Rossaint R et al, Crit Care 2023;27:80 (R33)

rescueRules: Give an antiemetic from a class that was not used for prophylaxis; repeating the same class within 6 hours adds no benefit.
After 6 hours, a second dose of a 5-HT₃ antagonist or a butyrophenone may be considered when no alternative is available.
Do not re-dose long-acting agents (aprepitant, fosaprepitant, palonosetron) in the PACU.
Amisulpride 10 mg IV was more effective than 5 mg for treatment after failed non-dopaminergic prophylaxis; propofol 20–40 mg is effective as treatment.

diastolic.validation: Validated against invasive pressures in 951 patients (Lababidi et al., Circulation 2025): accuracy 86%, with 2 indeterminate readings against 38 by the 2016 method.
diastolic.scope: Written for adults in sinus rhythm studied by transthoracic echo. The 2025 document says it should not be applied to children, to normal pregnancy, or in the intraoperative setting, and gives no TEE-specific cutoffs.
diastolic.readingWarning: Not for intraoperative use: the 2025 guideline says this algorithm should not be applied in the intraoperative setting, in children or in normal pregnancy. Use it to read a preoperative transthoracic study.
diastolic.supersedes: Replaces the 2016 ASE/EACVI recommendations. The 2025 approach uses one algorithm for any LVEF: e′, E/e′ and PASP or TR velocity first; LA strain, pulmonary vein flow, LA volume and IVRT when they disagree.

populations.name: Moderate or severe mitral annular calcification
notes: Figure 4: E/A below 0.8 means normal LAP and above 1.8 increased LAP; between them, IVRT of 80 ms or more means normal and under 80 ms increased.
e′ and E/e′ are not used with annular calcification.

populations.name: Heart transplant
notes: E/A of 2 or more with a preserved EF is common after transplant; pulmonary vein S/D does not help, and LA reservoir strain should not be used.
SRIVR is the LV strain rate during isovolumic relaxation, averaged from the three apical views; E/SRIVR is in cm.

populations.name: Atrial fibrillation or flutter
indicators: Deceleration time under 160 ms with depressed LVEF
Peak acceleration rate of mitral E 1,900 cm/s² or more
Deceleration time of the pulmonary venous diastolic velocity 220 ms or less
notes: Table 7 lists these as indicators of increased filling pressure in AF.
LA reservoir strain should not be used in AF; E/A and the A wave do not apply, and LA size is not a valid marker.
The 2025 document's dedicated AF algorithm is not built into this tool.

populations.name: Mitral stenosis
notes: E/e′ is not useful in mitral stenosis.

populations.name: Severe primary mitral regurgitation
indicators: Average E/e′ above 14, only with depressed EF
notes: E/e′ is not useful in primary MR with a normal EF, and LA reservoir strain should not be used in significant MR.
Measure time intervals over several beats with matched RR intervals.

populations.name: After mitral repair, replacement or TEER
indicators: Time intervals and PA pressures may help after repair or replacement
After TEER: LAP = 4V² + RAP across the iatrogenic atrial septal shunt; a shunt velocity above 1.7 m/s usually means increased LAP
notes: e′ and E/e′ are not accurate with a prosthetic mitral valve or an annuloplasty ring.

populations.name: LV assist device
indicators: Average E/e′ above 14 or septal E/e′ 15 or more
LA maximum volume index above 33 mL/m²
Interatrial septum: neutral, LAP about equal to RAP; bowing toward the right atrium, LAP about 5 mmHg above RAP; bowing toward the left atrium, about 5 mmHg below
notes: Table 7 lists these as indicators of increased filling pressure with an LVAD.

populations.name: Pulmonary hypertension without left heart disease
indicators: E/A 2 or more favors postcapillary PH; 0.8 or less favors precapillary PH
With E/A between 0.8 and 2: lateral E/e′ above 13, LA volume index above 34 mL/m² and LA reservoir strain under 18% favor postcapillary PH
notes: TR velocity and PASP stand in for LAP only without lung parenchymal or pulmonary vascular disease.
The 2025 document's dedicated PH algorithm is not built into this tool.

populations.name: Constrictive pericarditis
notes: Excluded from the main algorithm: e′ and E/e′ are inaccurate in pericardial disease.
The 2025 document's constriction criteria are not built into this tool.

populations.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
indicators: LA maximum volume index above 34 mL/m²
notes: Table 7 indicators of increased filling pressure in HCM, shown alongside the main algorithm.

populations.name: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
indicators: Deceleration time under 140 ms (specific, not sensitive)
notes: Table 7 indicators, shown alongside the main algorithm.

populations.name: Sinus tachycardia or fused E and A
indicators: Predominant early filling with depressed LVEF
Pulmonary vein systolic filling fraction 40% or less (specificity 88%)
Average E/e′ above 14 (high specificity, low sensitivity)
notes: E/A is unreliable when E at the onset of A is above 20 cm/s; a compensatory pause after an ectopic beat often separates E and A.

populations.name: Aortic regurgitation
indicators: LA enlargement, average E/e′ above 14, LA reservoir strain under 18% and TR above 2.8 m/s support increased filling pressure
Acute severe AR: premature mitral valve closure and diastolic MR mean increased LV filling pressure
notes: Keep the AR jet out of the mitral inflow sample.

exercise: Exertional symptoms with grade 1, or with filling pressure not determined at rest; completely normal function with preserved e′ needs no stress test
Average E/e′ 14 or more (or septal 15 or more) with peak TR velocity above 3.2 m/s
Average (or septal) E/e′ under 10 with TR velocity under 2.8 m/s
E/e′ above 14 with TR velocity above 2.8 but under 3.2 m/s
E/e′ under 14, even when TR velocity rises above 3.2 m/s
notes: Where the document's figures, tables and text differ by an equals sign, the tool follows Figure 3: E/e′ ≥ 14 (Figure 2 and the text: > 14), LARS ≤ 18% (elsewhere < 18%), e′ ≤ 6, 7 or 6.5 cm/s (Table 6 and Key Point 2: below), Ar − A > 30 ms (Table 7: ≥ 30) and TR ≥ 2.8 m/s (Table 7: > 2.8). With an age band picked, Table 6's 'below' applies, so over 65 a septal e′ of exactly 6 counts as normal. Figure 4's 0.8–1.8 band (Table 7: above 0.8 and below 1.8) and the transplant band of 7–14 (Table 7 leaves exactly 7 and 14 unassigned) keep their edges in the middle. A value exactly on a cutoff deserves a second look.

With both e′ sites measured, the average decides e′ (≤ 6.5 cm/s) and E/e′ (≥ 14); a single site's cutoff (e′ septal ≤ 6 or lateral ≤ 7 cm/s; E/e′ septal ≥ 15 or lateral ≥ 13) applies only when that is the one site measured. Figure 3 lists the three joined by 'or' and does not say how to weigh discordant sites.
Report mitral E, A, E/A, e′, average E/e′ and peak TR velocity, plus whichever supplemental measures decided the reading; if the grade cannot be set, report the filling pressure.

With one of the three main variables missing, the guideline gives no rule. The tool reads every way the missing one could fall and reports only a reading they all share, with a grade only when every way gives the same grade.

A pulmonary vein S/D above 0.67 counts as an absent sign only when LVEF is entered and below 50%: the ratio is reliable mainly with reduced LVEF and can exceed 0.67 despite raised filling pressure when LVEF is normal (p. 554). The guideline names no LVEF cutoff; the tool uses 50%. Table 4 also limits the ratio in AF, mitral valve disease and HCM.

LA reservoir strain should not be used with AF, significant MR, after heart transplant, with a normal EF and GLS above 18%, or with suspected LA stunning; with a normal LVEF a value above 18% does not rule out raised LAP (Table 4, p. 554).

Ar − A above 30 ms on its own is read as an isolated rise in LVEDP, as the text says (p. 552, footnote d), although Figure 3 lists it among the signs of increased LAP. Footnote d also asks for a pulmonary vein Ar velocity above 35 cm/s; the tool does not ask for it, nor for premature termination of mitral inflow or diastolic MR (footnote c).

measures.note: The upper limit is 2 SD above the predicted mean for age and sex at the reference BSA (men 2.0, women 1.7 m²), moved 0.5 mm for each 0.1 m² of BSA; at or above it the root is dilated (z-score of 2 or more).

groups.note: Lang 2015 Table 14 means (± SD), men and women: annulus 2.6 ± 0.3 and 2.3 ± 0.2 cm; sinuses 3.4 ± 0.3 and 3.0 ± 0.3 cm; sinotubular junction 2.9 ± 0.3 and 2.6 ± 0.3 cm; proximal ascending aorta 3.0 ± 0.4 and 2.7 ± 0.4 cm.

ivc.method: Subcostal view, end-expiration, 0.5–3 cm from the RA junction
notes: Secondary signs of raised RA pressure: RA enlargement, the interatrial septum bowing into the LA throughout the cycle, restrictive RV filling, tricuspid E/e′ above 6, diastolic predominance of hepatic vein flow (systolic filling fraction below 55%).
An IVC above 2.5 cm without respiratory variation, with spontaneous contrast or colour-flow reflux: 20 mmHg can be considered. A small, collapsed IVC suggests RA pressure below 3 mmHg (hypovolemia).

On positive-pressure ventilation the collapse cannot be used. An IVC of 1.2 cm or less in an intubated patient identifies RA pressure below 10 mmHg (ASE 2010); the 2025 update prints 2.1 cm for the same statement, and the tool keeps the stricter value.
A dilated IVC can be normal in young adults and athletes.

Normal ranges come from transthoracic studies in healthy adults; severity partitions, the tricuspid annulus threshold and the IVC scheme are consensus or literature based. None of these guidelines gives TEE-specific values, so applying them to intraoperative TEE is an extrapolation.

The source tables print whole numbers or one decimal, so a value between two printed ranges (an LVEF of 51–52% in men, an LA volume index of 34–35 mL/m², a septum of 1.05 cm in men) is read as the worse grade.
Body surface area by DuBois & DuBois; the guidelines do not name a formula.

The ASE 2025 right-heart guideline replaces the 2010 one; RV and RA cutoffs here follow Table 1 of its corrected May 2025 file, which differs from the March 2025 publisher PDF in a few cells (TAPSE, S′ and RA volume grades).

modes.name: Cardiac arrest
modes.cycleText: Rhythm check now: pause compressions under 10 seconds, switch compressors, then log the rhythm.
modes.note: AHA 2025: one shock at a time, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes (every second cycle after the first dose), amiodarone or lidocaine after the third shock. Adults: vasopressin, routine calcium, bicarbonate and magnesium are not recommended (Part 9). Children: routine calcium and bicarbonate are not recommended (Part 8).

groups.title: Treat
groups.note: Lidocaine for adults is per kg: 1–1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5–0.75 mg/kg. Child doses need the weight above.

prompts.text: Start CPR: push at least 5 cm at 100–120/min, 30:2 without an advanced airway; bag-mask ventilation with oxygen; attach the monitor-defibrillator. Log the first rhythm.

Start CPR: at least one-third of the chest depth at 100–120/min; 15:2 with two rescuers before puberty, 30:2 after puberty or alone; bag-mask ventilation with oxygen; attach the monitor-defibrillator. Log the first rhythm.
Shock now: {energy:shock}. Resume compressions straight after; the next rhythm check is in 2 minutes.
Epinephrine as soon as possible: {dose:epi}.
Two shocks have not worked: epinephrine {dose:epi}.
Epinephrine due (every 3–5 minutes): {dose:epi}.
Three shocks have not worked: amiodarone {dose:amio}, or lidocaine {dose:lido}.
If VF/pVT persists, a second amiodarone dose: {dose:amio}. The algorithm prints no interval for it.
If VF/pVT persists, a second lidocaine dose: {dose:lido}. The algorithm prints no interval for it.
Consider an advanced airway (ET tube or supraglottic) with continuous waveform capnography.
With the advanced airway: 1 breath every 6 seconds (10/min) with continuous compressions. A sudden rise in ETCO₂ can signal ROSC.
With the advanced airway: 1 breath every 2–3 seconds (20–30/min) with continuous compressions. Diastolic pressure on an arterial line: at least 25 mmHg in infants, 30 mmHg in children.
Work through the reversible causes below.

modes.name: After cardiac surgery
modes.patientNote: STS 2017 applies to all cardiac-surgical ICU patients, children included, but its drug doses are adult doses, so this tab is set for adults; resternotomy is part of the protocol until postoperative day 10. For children, AHA 2025 advises compressions when resternotomy is not at hand, early resternotomy, internal massage and ECLS; use the Arrest tab's doses.
modes.note: STS 2017 protocol: VF gets up to three stacked shocks, asystole gets pacing, PEA gets a quick search for reversible causes; compressions may wait at most 1 minute for these, and the chest is reopened within 5 minutes. Full-dose epinephrine and atropine are not routine.

groups.title: Rhythm
groups.note: No 10-second pulse check: VF or asystole on the monitor, or a flat arterial trace without an ETCO₂ waveform, is an arrest (STS).

groups.title: Drugs
groups.note: Epinephrine policy differs: STS 2017 gives no epinephrine or vasopressin during the arrest unless an experienced clinician directs it; ERC 2025 gives 50–100 mcg; AHA 2025 says nothing specific for this setting (its default is 1 mg every 3–5 minutes). Follow local policy and log what was given.

deadlines.label: Compressions unless shocks or pacing restore output

prompts.text: Confirm the arrest from the monitor and the arterial and ETCO₂ traces, call the arrest, and log the rhythm. Assign the six roles below.
VF/pVT: three stacked shocks now if the defibrillator is ready within a minute ({energy:cshock}); otherwise start compressions.
Three shocks have failed: compressions, then open the chest. Amiodarone {dose:amio} through a central line (lidocaine {dose:lido} is the alternative).
Asystole or severe bradycardia: pace through the epicardial wires now (DDD 80–100/min, maximum output). No wires, or no capture within a minute: start compressions, then transcutaneous pacing.

PEA: if paced, pause the pacemaker briefly to exclude VF. Exclude quickly reversible causes (tension pneumothorax, airway and ventilation, pacing), then reopen within 5 minutes; tamponade and bleeding are treated by reopening.
One minute: shocks or pacing have not restored output, so start external compressions at 100–120/min, aiming for a systolic above 60 mmHg.
A systolic under 60 mmHg with compressions means tamponade or hypovolemia until proved otherwise: reopen now.
Five minutes: emergency resternotomy now.
Chest open: two-handed internal massage at 100–120/min to a systolic above 60 mmHg; internal defibrillation as appropriate.

Disconnect the ventilator and hand-ventilate with 100% oxygen, removing PEEP; check both sides for breath sounds and chest movement and the ETCO₂ trace. Suspected tension pneumothorax: needle in the 2nd intercostal space, midclavicular line.
Stop all pre-arrest infusions; sedation may continue if awareness is a concern.
