manual.note: Stanford's Obstetric Anesthesia Emergency Manual (Seligman, Chu, Abir) is shared under a no-derivatives license, so this tool is built from the primary sources instead; open the manual for Stanford's own checklists.

events.title: Maternal Cardiac Arrest
events.summary: Standard ALS with continuous left uterine displacement, airway early, IV above the diaphragm, and resuscitative delivery by 5 minutes if there is no return of circulation (fundus at or above the umbilicus; SOAP and OAA: 20 weeks or more).

timer.label: Since the arrest

marks.text: No ROSC, fundus at or above the umbilicus (SOAP and OAA: 20 weeks or more): start the resuscitative hysterotomy where she is (SOAP 2014: incision at 4 minutes; SMFM 2026: begin within 4 minutes).
Baby delivered by 5 minutes if there is no ROSC (AHA 2025), when the fundus is at or above the umbilicus.

timer.note: Start it at the moment of arrest. Prepare for delivery from the start; do not move her to an operating room.

weightDoses.label: Lidocaine, first dose
weightDoses.note: Second dose 0.5–0.75 mg/kg (adult ALS)

sections.heading: Recognize
items: A pregnant or recently delivered patient without a pulse: recognition and CPR are standard BLS and ALS.

Causes, A to H (AHA): anesthetic complications (high neuraxial block, airway loss, aspiration, LAST), bleeding, cardiovascular, drugs (oxytocin, magnesium), embolic (amniotic fluid, pulmonary), fever, general (Hs and Ts), hypertension (preeclampsia, eclampsia).

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Call the obstetric arrest team with one activation that also brings the neonatal team; name a leader, a timekeeper, an airway lead, compressors and one person for uterine displacement.
High-quality CPR: 100–120/min, at least 5 cm, hands on the lower half of the sternum.
Continuous manual left uterine displacement whenever the fundus is at or above the umbilicus.
Defibrillate at the usual adult energies; take off fetal monitors, but never delay a shock for them.
Airway early, by the most experienced person (expect a difficult airway); 100% oxygen, waveform capnography.
IV or IO access above the diaphragm.
Magnesium running: stop it and give calcium.
Amniotic fluid embolism suspected: activate the massive transfusion protocol; balanced red cells, plasma and platelets.
Start the clock above; with the fundus at or above the umbilicus (SOAP and OAA: 20 weeks or more), prepare for resuscitative delivery at the bedside from the start.
Consider extracorporeal CPR where it is available (AHA 2025: reasonable).
After delivery the neonatal team resuscitates the baby; continue maternal ALS and look for the cause.

sections.heading: Drugs
rows: Stop it and give IV calcium; the AHA 2025 algorithm prints no dose. OAA card 1-1: calcium chloride 10% 10 mL IV; the equivalent is calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL (ALSO 2017, adapted from AHA 2015)
Lipid emulsion 20%: see the LAST tab
sections.note: No drug is withheld or changed for the fetus (AHA 2015).

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Do not take her to the operating room to deliver: deliver where she is (SMFM 2026 allows a transfer only if it takes 1–2 minutes).
Cricoid pressure is not routine during the arrest airway (AHA 2015).
After delivery, large oxytocin boluses can cause collapse or re-arrest.

sections.heading: Where Sources Differ
items: Delivery: AHA 2025 by 5 minutes when the fundus is at or above the umbilicus; SOAP 2014 incision at 4 and delivery at 5 minutes beyond 20 weeks; SMFM 2016 immediate delivery from 23 weeks; SMFM 2026 start within 4 minutes.
Hand position: AHA 2015 lower half of the sternum; SOAP 2014 repeats the older advice of 2–3 cm higher.

events.title: Postpartum Hemorrhage
events.summary: Stage it out loud, measure the blood loss, uterotonics and massage, tranexamic acid within 3 hours, and blood without waiting for labs.

sections.heading: Recognize
items: Hemorrhage (ACOG, as summarized by AAFP 2023): cumulative loss of 1000 mL or more, or any loss with signs of hypovolemia, within 24 hours of birth.
Stage 1: over 500 mL after vaginal or over 1000 mL after cesarean birth, or a vital-sign change (CMQCC: by more than 15%, or heart rate 110 or more, BP 85/45 or less, SpO₂ under 95%).

Stage 2: bleeding continuing up to 1500 mL, or more than two uterotonics needed. Stage 3: over 1500 mL, more than 2 units of red cells, unstable vital signs or suspected coagulopathy. Stage 4: cardiovascular collapse.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Declare the stage, call for help, activate the hemorrhage protocol; quantify the blood loss continuously.
Two large-bore IVs (16–18 G); type and crossmatch; send CBC, coagulation tests and fibrinogen.
Oxytocin infusion, vigorous fundal massage, empty the bladder.
Second-line uterotonic chosen by contraindication: methylergonovine (not if hypertensive), carboprost (not if asthmatic), misoprostol.
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV at 1 mL/min (10–20 minutes), within 3 hours of birth; a second 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 minutes or restarts within 24 hours.
Stage 2: transfuse on clinical grounds, without waiting for results; 2 units of red cells in the room; thaw plasma.
Stage 3: massive transfusion protocol, red cells to plasma near 1:1, a platelet pack per 4–6 units (CMQCC); cryoprecipitate for coagulopathy.
Check and treat low calcium during transfusion; warm the patient and fluids; cell salvage and viscoelastic testing where available.
Escalate with the obstetric team to balloon tamponade, compression sutures, embolization or hysterectomy.

sections.heading: Uterotonics
rows: 10–40 units in 500–1000 mL as an infusion; 10 units IM if no IV
Every 15–90 min, at most 8 doses (2 mg)
800–1000 mcg PR, 800 mcg SL or 600 mcg PO (SMI 2015)
1 g IV at 1 mL/min, never faster (10–20 min)
1 g after 30 min if bleeding continues, or if it restarts within 24 h
First dose after 3 h: no benefit
sections.note: Methylergonovine repeat interval is from its label; the other values are from the SMI 2015 checklist, CMQCC, the Indiana uterotonic chart and FIGO/ICM.

sections.heading: Calcium and Blood
rows: OAA: calcium chloride 10% 10 mL or calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL IV
Red cells to plasma near 1:1; 1 apheresis platelet pack per 4–6 units of red cells (CMQCC 2014)
A fibrinogen target and cryoprecipitate dose (ACOG PB 183 could not be read)

sections.heading: Cautions
items: A normal hemoglobin before adequate fluid resuscitation is falsely reassuring.
Tranexamic acid faster than 1 mL/min can cause hypotension (FIGO/ICM).

sections.heading: Where Sources Differ
items: Misoprostol: CMQCC 800 mcg SL; OAA 1000 mcg PR or 800 mcg SL; the Indiana chart 600–800 mcg SL, PO or PR once.
Carboprost interval: 15–90 minutes (label) or every 15 minutes (SMI, OAA); all agree on 8 doses at most.
Oxytocin: US charts give an infusion without a bolus; OAA (UK) gives 5 IU slowly IV, up to twice, then 40 IU in 50 mL at 12.5 mL/h.
Thresholds: US staging at 500, 1000 and 1500 mL; UK major over 1.5 L, massive over 2.5 L.

events.title: Severe Hypertension and Eclampsia
events.summary: Treat a confirmed severe-range pressure within 30–60 minutes; magnesium for seizures; protect the airway.

weightDoses.label: Levetiracetam (persistent seizure)
weightDoses.note: Single source (eclampsia algorithm)

weightDoses.label: Fosphenytoin (persistent seizure)
weightDoses.note: At 150 mg PE/min; single source

sections.heading: Recognize
items: Severe range: systolic 160 or more, or diastolic 110 or more, confirmed within 15 minutes: a hypertensive emergency.
Warning signs: severe headache, visual change, epigastric or right upper quadrant pain, altered mental status, new breathlessness. Eclampsia: a seizure in this setting.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Seizure: call for help, protect her, left side (head of the bed down if pregnant), oxygen; prepare to intubate if seizures recur.
Magnesium sulfate: 4–6 g IV over 20–30 minutes, then 1–2 g/h. No IV: 10 g IM (5 g in each buttock), then 5 g IM every 4 hours.
Antihypertensive within 30–60 minutes of the confirmed reading; give it with magnesium, and first if only one can be given.
First-line: IV labetalol, IV hydralazine, or immediate-release oral nifedipine (nifedipine if no IV; hydralazine or nifedipine if asthma or bradycardia).
Not controlled after successive doses: emergency consultation (anesthesiology, maternal-fetal medicine, critical care); an infusion such as nicardipine with them.
Once controlled, aim for 130–150/80–100 mmHg; BP every 10 min for an hour, every 15 min for an hour, every 30 min for an hour, then hourly for 4 hours.
Recurrent seizure on magnesium: 2–4 g more IV over 5 minutes (CMQCC); still seizing, a benzodiazepine or another anticonvulsant; consider head imaging.
Watch for magnesium toxicity: lost reflexes, respiratory depression; check the level 4 hours after starting.
Plan delivery once she is stable; continue magnesium at least 24–48 hours after the last seizure or after delivery, whichever is later (ACOG 2023).

sections.heading: Antihypertensive Pathways
rows: 20 mg IV over 2 min, then 40 mg, then 80 mg
Hydralazine 10 mg IV, recheck at 20 min, then consult
5 or 10 mg IV over 2 min, then 10 mg
Labetalol 20 mg IV (10 min), then 40 mg and consult
10 mg PO, then 20 mg, then 20 mg
sections.note: 24-hour maximums: hydralazine 25 mg IV (SMI 2019, Texas 2025); labetalol 300 mg IV (SMI 2020, Texas 2025) or 220 mg (SMI 2019). Hold labetalol if the pulse is under 60 (SMI 2020; Texas 2025: under 70). Swallow nifedipine whole, never sublingual (SMI 2019).

sections.heading: Magnesium and Seizures
rows: 4–6 g IV over 20–30 min (CMQCC: 6 g if BMI over 35)
2–4 g IV over 5 min (CMQCC; UK 2 g); lorazepam 4 mg IV (ACOG 2023) or 2–4 mg (SMI 2019); diazepam 5–10 mg IV to 30 mg; midazolam 10 mg IM if no IV
Calcium gluconate 10% 10 mL (1 g) IV over 3 min (ACOG 2023)
Therapeutic 4.9–8.5; reflexes lost 8.5–12.2; respiratory paralysis 12.2–15.8; stop the infusion above 9.6, restart below 8.4 (ACOG 2023 algorithm)
2.5–5 mg/h, titrate, maximum 15 mg/h, with the consultant (Nationwide Children's pathway, single source)

sections.heading: Cautions
items: No methylergonovine in hypertension or preeclampsia.
Magnesium: contraindicated in myasthenia gravis (SMI 2019); reduce in renal impairment; magnesium with nifedipine can drop the pressure fast (OAA).

sections.heading: Where Sources Differ
items: Labetalol 24-hour maximum: 300 mg (SMI 2020, Texas 2025) or 220 mg (SMI 2019).
Magnesium: US load over 20–30 min with 1–2 g/h (Texas 2025: 2 g/h); UK 4 g over 5 min with 1 g/h.
UK first-line regimens differ (oral labetalol 200 mg; IV labetalol 50 mg every 5 min to 200 mg).

events.title: High or Total Neuraxial Block
events.summary: Oxygenate and ventilate, support the circulation with uterine displacement and vasopressors, and secure the airway early.

sections.heading: Recognize
items: After any epidural, spinal or combined technique: difficulty breathing, weak arms or hands, hypotension and bradycardia, impaired consciousness, apnea (OAA, AAGBI).

It can come on fast, or late and slowly. Consider a vasovagal event, aortocaval compression, LAST, amniotic fluid embolism and concealed hemorrhage (OAA, AAGBI); subarachnoid hemorrhage (NHS Borders).

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Call for help and the airway and arrest trolleys; name a leader, a checklist reader and a scribe; reassure her: she may be aware.
High-flow oxygen; bag-mask ventilation if apneic or breathing poorly, then secure the airway (rapid-sequence, reduced hypnotic dose); a failed intubation follows the failed-intubation drill.
Uterine displacement; raise the legs but no head-down tilt; rapid fluid bolus with a vasopressor; anticholinergic for bradycardia; full monitoring.
Cardiac arrest: switch to the Arrest tab (delivery by 5 minutes).
Ventilated and possibly aware: give a hypnotic.
The obstetric team decides on delivery once she is stable.
Support breathing and circulation until the block wears off (about 4 hours, OAA); debrief with her later.

sections.heading: Drugs
rows: 50–100 mcg IV, then an infusion; no bolus if bradycardic
6–12 mg IV, repeated (tachyphylaxis; OAA maximum 30 mg)
500 mcg IV, repeat to 3 mg (OAA); 0.6–1.2 mg (AAGBI)
No source gives a dose short of arrest; in arrest 1 mg IV every 3–5 min

sections.heading: Cautions
items: No head-down tilt.
Sit her up only without cardiovascular compromise.

events.title: Amniotic Fluid Embolism
events.summary: Sudden collapse with hypoxia, hypotension and then coagulopathy: CPR and delivery if arrested, right-heart support, and early balanced blood products.

sections.heading: Recognize
items: Sudden cardiorespiratory collapse (hypoxia, hypotension), often followed by coagulopathy, in labor, at delivery or soon after.
A clinical diagnosis: no laboratory test confirms or excludes it (SMFM).

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Call for help (obstetrics, anesthesia, critical care, respiratory therapy, neonatal team); 100% oxygen, IV access, ventilatory support.
Pulseless: high-quality CPR with uterine displacement and the Arrest tab's clock; start the hysterotomy within 4 minutes if there is no ROSC (SMFM 2026).
Oxygenate and ventilate; vasopressors and inotropes as needed; avoid excess crystalloid (give blood products for volume).

Right-heart failure: dobutamine or milrinone, norepinephrine for hypotension, a pulmonary vasodilator (inhaled nitric oxide, prostacyclin); avoid hypoxia, acidosis and hypercapnia; guide with echocardiography.
Check coagulation early; massive transfusion without waiting for labs, about 1:1:1; keep platelets above 50,000; uterotonics and tranexamic acid.
Treat atony aggressively and look for genital-tract lacerations.
Refractory: consider ECMO (SMFM 2026); recombinant factor VIIa only as a last resort.
Assign timekeeping and blood-product records; report the case to the AFE registry.

sections.heading: Drugs
rows: 20 mg orally or by tube three times daily
sections.note: SMFM 2016 Table 2 as extracted printed 'mg/kg per minute'; SMFM's 2026 correction gives mcg/kg/min for these drugs, which is shown. Single source: check against the journal table.

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Volume overload worsens right-heart failure.
No evidence supports routine steroids.
SMFM 2026 cites an expert panel that recommends against routine use of the atropine–ondansetron–ketorolac ('A-OK') regimen; the evidence is case reports only.

sections.heading: Where Sources Differ
items: Plasma or cryoprecipitate: SMFM 2016 1:1:1 with plasma; SMFM 2026 favors cryoprecipitate to limit volume.
ECMO: not routine (2016); can be considered even with coagulopathy (2026).

events.title: Difficult or Failed Intubation
events.summary: Two attempts at most, then a supraglottic airway and oxygenation; decide wake or proceed by the plan agreed before induction.

weightDoses.label: Rocuronium (rapid sequence)
weightDoses.note: With sugammadex available

weightDoses.label: Sugammadex (immediate reversal)
weightDoses.note: Full reversal of rocuronium within 3 minutes (OAA/DAS)

sections.heading: Recognize
items: Failed intubation: not achieved after two attempts (a third only by an experienced anesthetist). Say it out loud.
Cannot oxygenate as well: a can't-intubate, can't-oxygenate emergency.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Before induction: airway and fasting assessment, antacid prophylaxis, checklist, senior help identified, equipment ready, and a wake-or-proceed decision agreed with the obstetric team.
Preoxygenate to an end-tidal oxygen of at least 0.9; consider nasal oxygen during apnea.
Rapid sequence: an adequate dose of induction agent, suxamethonium or rocuronium 1–1.2 mg/kg; cricoid pressure 10 N rising to 30 N.
Gentle mask ventilation is allowed (peak pressure under 20 cmH₂O).
Laryngoscopy at most twice, optimizing between attempts (cricoid, position, bougie, a different laryngoscope).
Failed: call for help; second-generation supraglottic airway, cricoid released during insertion, at most two attempts; otherwise two-person mask ventilation.
Wake or proceed by the plan. Waking: keep oxygenating, head up or left lateral, sugammadex to reverse rocuronium.
Proceeding: maintain anesthesia and ventilation, gastric tube through the airway, minimal fundal pressure, senior obstetrician operating; tell the neonatal team about the failed intubation.
Can't intubate, can't oxygenate: declare it, 100% oxygen, full paralysis, front-of-neck access; arrest means the Arrest tab.

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Release cricoid pressure while inserting a supraglottic airway, and if mask ventilation is difficult.
Repeated attempts injure the airway: stop at the limits.
Give an adequate induction dose: OAA/DAS cites NAP5 on thiopental under 4 mg/kg as too low.

sections.heading: Where Sources Differ
items: Cricoid pressure: OAA/DAS uses it for obstetric induction; AHA 2015 does not recommend it routinely during arrest.

events.title: Local Anesthetic Toxicity in Pregnancy
events.summary: Stop the local anesthetic, airway and seizure control, lipid emulsion early, modified ALS with uterine displacement and delivery if arrested.

weightDoses.label: Lipid 20% bolus over 2–3 min
weightDoses.note: Weight basis not stated (ASRA 2020, OAA); SOAP 2014: ideal body weight. Repeat if still unstable (OAA: at 5 and 10 min)

weightDoses.label: Lipid infusion
weightDoses.note: 0.25 mL/kg/min; double if still unstable (ASRA 2020; 2017 advisory: 200–250 mL over 70 kg)

weightDoses.label: Lipid upper limit
weightDoses.note: About 12 mL/kg (ASRA, OAA); SOAP 2014: about 10 mL/kg over 30 min

weightDoses.label: Lorazepam (seizures)
weightDoses.note: OAA; repeat after 5 min

sections.heading: Recognize
items: Central: sudden change in mental state, agitation, loss of consciousness, seizures. Cardiovascular: bradycardia, conduction block, ventricular arrhythmias, hypotension, collapse.
It may occur some time after the initial injection (OAA).

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Stop all local anesthetic, epidural pumps included; call for help, the LAST kit and the arrest trolley; alert a bypass or ECMO team early.
Airway and oxygen; avoid hypercarbia. Left lateral, or supine with manual uterine displacement.
Seizures: a benzodiazepine; propofol only in small doses if nothing else (ASRA 2020), never with cardiovascular compromise (ASRA 2017).
Lipid emulsion 20% at the first serious sign: the doses for her weight are above.
Still unstable: repeat the bolus and double the infusion, within 12 mL/kg in all.

Arrest: CPR with small epinephrine doses (1 mcg/kg or less), no vasopressin, calcium-channel blockers, beta-blockers or lidocaine; continue lipid; the Arrest tab's clock for delivery; expect a long resuscitation.
Continue lipid more than 15 minutes after stability; monitor 2 hours after a seizure, 4–6 hours after cardiovascular instability.

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Propofol is not a substitute for lipid.
The ASRA checklist has no pregnancy-specific changes; delivery timing comes from the obstetric arrest guidance.

sections.heading: Where Sources Differ
items: Lipid limit: 12 mL/kg (ASRA, OAA) or about 10 mL/kg over 30 minutes (SOAP 2014).
Weight: ASRA 2017 uses ideal body weight for the under-70 kg infusion; SOAP 2014 for bolus and infusion; ASRA 2020 and OAA do not state one.

events.title: Maternal Sepsis and Septic Shock
events.summary: Cultures and antibiotics within an hour, 1–2 L of balanced crystalloid, norepinephrine for shock, and source control.

sections.heading: Recognize
items: Unexplained organ dysfunction with suspected infection, with or without fever, in pregnancy or after birth.
Septic shock: vasopressors needed to keep the MAP at 65 mmHg, with lactate over 2 mmol/L despite adequate volume.
No single screening tool is adequate in pregnancy (qSOFA is 50% sensitive); lactate over 2 mmol/L is common in labor.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Treat as an emergency: the first bundle within 1 hour in shock, within 3 hours otherwise.
Blood cultures before antibiotics, if that does not delay them; measure lactate.
Broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour in septic shock or a high likelihood of sepsis, chosen by the likely source.
Hypotension or hypoperfusion: 1–2 L of balanced crystalloid within 3 hours, reassessing the response; no starches or gelatins.
Septic shock: norepinephrine first, MAP 65 mmHg; vasopressin second; dobutamine or epinephrine for myocardial dysfunction.
Find and control the source; if it is the uterus, deliver or evacuate it regardless of gestation.
Norepinephrine or epinephrine still at 0.25 mcg/kg/min or more 4 hours after starting: hydrocortisone 50 mg IV every 6 hours. VTE prophylaxis; insulin above 180 mg/dL.

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Pregnancy is prone to pulmonary edema: SMFM notes 30 mL/kg may be too aggressive.
Sepsis alone is not a reason for immediate delivery, except intra-amniotic infection.

events.title: Umbilical Cord Prolapse
events.summary: Relieve cord compression and deliver fast; general anesthesia if the fetus is compromised.

sections.heading: Recognize
items: The cord felt or seen at or beyond the presenting part after membrane rupture, often with sudden fetal bradycardia.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Call the obstetrician, anesthesiologist and neonatal team; move toward the operating room with continuous fetal monitoring.

Relieve compression: elevate the presenting part by hand or by filling the bladder (500–750 mL saline, then clamp); knee-chest or exaggerated left lateral position; handle the cord as little as possible.
Fetal heart still abnormal: consider terbutaline 0.25 mg subcutaneously while preparing.
Category 1 cesarean, birth within 30 minutes if the trace is abnormal; operative vaginal birth if fully dilated and quick.

Anesthesia agreed with the obstetric team: general anesthesia with fetal compromise; regional in the lateral position if the fetal heart is reassuring; no repeated regional attempts. Be ready for general anesthesia either way.
Empty the filled bladder before any attempt at birth.

sections.heading: Where Sources Differ
items: Terbutaline: 0.25 mg (RCOG, OAA) or 500 mcg (NHS Lanarkshire 2024). Bladder filling: 500–750 mL (RCOG) or 500 mL (OAA).

events.title: Uterine Rupture
events.summary: Fetal bradycardia and new pain in labor after a cesarean: emergency laparotomy and massive hemorrhage resuscitation.

sections.heading: Recognize
items: Most often fetal bradycardia or decelerations; also abdominal pain out of proportion, breakthrough pain through a working epidural, vaginal bleeding, loss of station, instability, hematuria.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Call for help; emergency cesarean or laparotomy with repair or hysterectomy (obstetric decision).
A working epidural may be extended if she is stable and time allows; be ready to convert to general anesthesia.

Massive hemorrhage: oxygen, two large-bore IVs, bloods and crossmatch, tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 minutes (repeat after 30 if bleeding), early blood products, calcium, warming: see the Hemorrhage tab.
Arrest: the Arrest tab.

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Breakthrough pain during a trial of labor after cesarean can be rupture: think of it before simply re-dosing the epidural.

events.title: Shoulder Dystocia
events.summary: The obstetric team works the maneuvers; anesthesia stands ready for cephalic replacement and the hemorrhage and neonate that follow.

sections.heading: Recognize
items: The head delivered but the shoulders do not with routine traction.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Call the senior obstetrician, anesthesiologist and neonatal team; the obstetric team performs the maneuvers.
Be ready for urgent general or regional anesthesia in case of cephalic replacement (Zavanelli) and cesarean.
Before replacement, a uterine relaxant: terbutaline 0.25 mg subcutaneously, or sublingual nitroglycerin spray.
After birth, expect postpartum hemorrhage and neonatal resuscitation.

sections.heading: Uterine Relaxants
rows: No society dose exists. Reports: 50–100 mcg IV (1997 letter); 400–800 mcg sublingual (case report, letter)

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Relaxants can cause hypotension (Hicks 2000).

events.title: Uterine Inversion
events.summary: Replace the uterus at once, treat shock (it may be vagal), relax the uterus if needed, then uterotonics.

sections.heading: Recognize
items: The fundus inverted into or through the cervix after birth, with hemorrhage and shock that may be bradycardic (vagal), hypovolemic, or both.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Call for help; lie her flat; oxygen; two large-bore IVs; bloods and crossmatch; resuscitate during the first replacement attempt.
Leave an attached placenta in place until the uterus is replaced.
Immediate manual replacement by the obstetrician; if it fails, to the operating room.
Bradycardic shock: atropine 0.5 mg IV, repeated to 3 mg. Hypovolemic shock: warmed fluid and blood (Hemorrhage tab).
A tight cervical ring: terbutaline 0.25 mg subcutaneously or sublingual nitroglycerin; general anesthesia with a volatile agent if those fail.
Avoid a phenylephrine bolus, above all if bradycardic.
Manual replacement fails: hydrostatic replacement (warm saline), then laparotomy.
Once replaced: start oxytocin, remove the placenta in theatre, antibiotics; atonic hemorrhage follows in over 90% (OAA).

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Exclude uterine rupture before hydrostatic replacement.

events.title: Newborn Resuscitation

weightFor.title: Newborn Weight
weightFor.prompt: Enter the newborn's weight, not the mother's: the doses below are per kilogram until you do.
weightFor.maxText: That is not a newborn's weight. Enter the newborn's weight, not the mother's.

events.summary: Warm, dry and stimulate; ventilate within 60 seconds if not breathing or the heart rate is under 100; compressions and epinephrine under 60.

weightDoses.label: Epinephrine IV or IO (UVC)
weightDoses.note: Every 3–5 min; 0.1–0.3 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL

weightDoses.label: Epinephrine endotracheal
weightDoses.note: Only until vascular access; 0.5–1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL

weightDoses.label: Volume (saline or blood)
weightDoses.note: Over 5–10 min for suspected hypovolemia

sections.heading: At Birth
items: Term? Good tone? Breathing or crying? All yes: skin to skin. Any no: start the steps below within the first minute.
Defer cord clamping at least 60 seconds when feasible.

sections.heading: Do Now
items: Warm, dry, position the airway, stimulate; clear the airway only if needed; temperature 36.5–37.5 °C.
Apneic, gasping or heart rate under 100: positive-pressure ventilation within 60 seconds, 30–60 breaths/min, pulse oximetry; 21% oxygen from 35 weeks (21–30% at 32–34 weeks, 30–100% under 32).
Heart rate still under 100: ventilation corrective steps; consider a tube or laryngeal mask.
Heart rate under 60 after 30 seconds of effective ventilation: secure the airway, compressions 3:1 with ventilation, 100% oxygen, umbilical venous or IO access.
Still under 60: epinephrine every 3–5 minutes; consider hypovolemia and pneumothorax.

sections.heading: Cautions
items: Newborn epinephrine is per kilogram: never the adult 1 mg.
